docs.title: Alerts v3: Category Hub Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For Claude: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task.

Goal: Restructure /alerts into a mission-control category hub with 13 alert categories, sub-categories, MITRE ATT&CK mapping, and dedicated /alerts/[category] drill-down pages.

Architecture: Backend-first approach. Extend alert_intelligence.py with 6 new categories + sub-categories + MITRE mapping. Enhance the /api/alerts/categories endpoint to return rich data. Add new /api/alerts/categories/{cat} and /api/alerts/categories/{cat}/timeline endpoints. Then rebuild the frontend: hub page with interactive category grid, and new category detail page. docs.text:

# New categories

def categorize_sub_category(signature: str, category: str) -> str:
    """Return sub-category key for the given signature within its parent category."""
    subs = SUB_CATEGORIES.get(category, {})
    sig_upper = signature.upper()
    for sub_key, sub_info in subs.items():
        for pattern in sub_info.get("patterns", []):
            if pattern.upper() in sig_upper:
                return sub_key
    # Default: first sub-category if any exist, else empty string
    return next(iter(subs), "")

async def handle_alerts_categories(request: web.Request) -> web.Response:
    """GET /api/alerts/categories — Enhanced with sub-categories, severity, trend, sparkline."""
    client = _get_client(request)
    from_ts, to_ts = _parse_time_range(request)

    # Main query: group by signature, then we'll classify in Python
    query = {
        "size": 0,
        "query": {"bool": {"filter": _suricata_alert_filters(from_ts, to_ts)}},
        "aggs": {
            "by_signature": {
                "terms": {"field": "rule.name.keyword", "size": 500},
                "aggs": {
                    "severity": {"terms": {"field": "suricata.alert.severity", "size": 5}},
                    "over_time": {
                        "date_histogram": {"field": "@timestamp", "fixed_interval": _sparkline_interval(from_ts, to_ts), "min_doc_count": 0},
                    },
                },
            },
        },
    }

    try:
        result = await _os_search(client, query)
    except Exception as exc:
        return web.json_response({"error": str(exc)}, status=502)

    buckets = result.get("aggregations", {}).get("by_signature", {}).get("buckets", [])

    # Aggregate into categories
    from services.alert_intelligence import (
        THREAT_CATEGORIES, SUB_CATEGORIES, categorize_alert, categorize_sub_category,
        reclassify_severity, SEVERITY_NAMES,
    )

    cats: dict[str, dict] = {}
    for cat_id, cat_info in THREAT_CATEGORIES.items():
        cats[cat_id] = {
            "id": cat_id,
            "label": cat_info["label"],
            "icon": cat_info["icon"],
            "color": cat_info["color"],
            "description": cat_info["description"],
            "count": 0,
            "severity_breakdown": {"critical": 0, "high": 0, "medium": 0, "low": 0, "info": 0},
            "trend": {"direction": "stable", "percentage": 0},
            "sparkline": [],
            "sub_categories": {},
        }

    for bucket in buckets:
        sig = bucket["key"]
        count = bucket["doc_count"]
        cat_id = categorize_alert(sig)
        sub_id = categorize_sub_category(sig, cat_id)

        if cat_id not in cats:
            cat_id = "informational"

        cats[cat_id]["count"] += count

        # Severity breakdown
        for sev_bucket in bucket.get("severity", {}).get("buckets", []):
            sev_num = reclassify_severity(sig, sev_bucket["key"])
            sev_name = SEVERITY_NAMES.get(sev_num, "info")
            cats[cat_id]["severity_breakdown"][sev_name] = (
                cats[cat_id]["severity_breakdown"].get(sev_name, 0) + sev_bucket["doc_count"]
            )

        # Sub-category aggregation
        if sub_id:
            sub_info = SUB_CATEGORIES.get(cat_id, {}).get(sub_id, {})
            sub_label = sub_info.get("label", sub_id)
            if sub_id not in cats[cat_id]["sub_categories"]:
                cats[cat_id]["sub_categories"][sub_id] = {"id": sub_id, "label": sub_label, "count": 0}
            cats[cat_id]["sub_categories"][sub_id]["count"] += count

        # Sparkline: aggregate time buckets
        time_buckets = bucket.get("over_time", {}).get("buckets", [])
        if not cats[cat_id]["sparkline"]:
            cats[cat_id]["sparkline"] = [0] * len(time_buckets)
        for i, tb in enumerate(time_buckets):
            if i < len(cats[cat_id]["sparkline"]):
                cats[cat_id]["sparkline"][i] += tb["doc_count"]

    # Compute trends from sparkline data
    for cat in cats.values():
        spark = cat["sparkline"]
        if len(spark) >= 4:
            mid = len(spark) // 2
            first_half = sum(spark[:mid]) or 1
            second_half = sum(spark[mid:])
            pct = int(((second_half - first_half) / first_half) * 100)
            if pct > 10:
                cat["trend"] = {"direction": "increasing", "percentage": abs(pct)}
            elif pct < -10:
                cat["trend"] = {"direction": "decreasing", "percentage": abs(pct)}
            else:
                cat["trend"] = {"direction": "stable", "percentage": 0}
        # Convert sub_categories dict to sorted list
        cat["sub_categories"] = sorted(
            cat["sub_categories"].values(), key=lambda s: s["count"], reverse=True
        )

    # Sort categories by count descending
    result_list = sorted(cats.values(), key=lambda c: c["count"], reverse=True)

    return web.json_response({
        "from": from_ts, "to": to_ts,
        "categories": result_list,
    })

Add a helper to compute sparkline interval:

def _sparkline_interval(from_ts: str, to_ts: str) -> str:
    """Choose a sparkline interval that gives ~7 buckets."""
    from datetime import datetime
    try:
        f = datetime.fromisoformat(from_ts.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
        t = datetime.fromisoformat(to_ts.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
        delta = (t - f).total_seconds()
    except Exception:
        return "1h"
    if delta <= 3600:       return "5m"    # 15m→~3, 1h→~12
    if delta <= 14400:      return "30m"   # 4h→~8
    if delta <= 86400:      return "3h"    # 24h→~8
    if delta <= 604800:     return "1d"    # 7d→~7
    return "1d"

    if not cat_info:
        return web.json_response({"error": f"Unknown category: {cat_id}"}, status=404)

    # Gather all signatures that belong to this category
    patterns = cat_info.get("patterns", [])

    # Query: get all alerts, grouped by signature, src_ip, dst_ip
    query = {
        "size": 0,
        "query": {"bool": {"filter": _suricata_alert_filters(from_ts, to_ts)}},
        "aggs": {
            "by_signature": {
                "terms": {"field": "rule.name.keyword", "size": 200},
                "aggs": {
                    "by_src": {"terms": {"field": "source.ip.keyword", "size": 100}},
                    "by_dst": {"terms": {"field": "destination.ip.keyword", "size": 100}},
                    "severity": {"terms": {"field": "suricata.alert.severity", "size": 5}},
                    "last_seen": {"max": {"field": "@timestamp"}},
                },
            },
        },
    }

    try:
        result = await _os_search(client, query)
    except Exception as exc:
        return web.json_response({"error": str(exc)}, status=502)

    buckets = result.get("aggregations", {}).get("by_signature", {}).get("buckets", [])

    # Filter to only this category
    total = 0
    sources: set[str] = set()
    targets: set[str] = set()
    sub_cats: dict[str, int] = {}
    sev_breakdown = {"critical": 0, "high": 0, "medium": 0, "low": 0, "info": 0}
    signatures: list[dict] = []
    device_alerts: dict[str, int] = {}

    for bucket in buckets:
        sig = bucket["key"]
        if categorize_alert(sig) != cat_id:
            continue

        count = bucket["doc_count"]
        total += count
        sub_id = categorize_sub_category(sig, cat_id)

        if sub_id:
            sub_cats[sub_id] = sub_cats.get(sub_id, 0) + count

        for sev_b in bucket.get("severity", {}).get("buckets", []):
            sev_name = SEVERITY_NAMES.get(reclassify_severity(sig, sev_b["key"]), "info")
            sev_breakdown[sev_name] += sev_b["doc_count"]

        for src_b in bucket.get("by_src", {}).get("buckets", []):
            sources.add(src_b["key"])
        for dst_b in bucket.get("by_dst", {}).get("buckets", []):
            targets.add(dst_b["key"])
            device_alerts[dst_b["key"]] = device_alerts.get(dst_b["key"], 0) + dst_b["doc_count"]

        last_seen = bucket.get("last_seen", {}).get("value_as_string", "")
        signatures.append({"signature": sig, "count": count, "last_seen": last_seen})

    # Build sub-category list
    sub_info = SUB_CATEGORIES.get(cat_id, {})
    sub_list = []
    for sub_id, sub_count in sorted(sub_cats.items(), key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True):
        si = sub_info.get(sub_id, {})
        sub_list.append({"id": sub_id, "label": si.get("label", sub_id), "count": sub_count})

    # Build affected devices list (top 20)
    device_list = sorted(
        [{"ip": ip, "count": c} for ip, c in device_alerts.items()],
        key=lambda d: d["count"], reverse=True,
    )[:20]

    # Sort signatures
    signatures.sort(key=lambda s: s["count"], reverse=True)

    mitre_tactic = cat_info.get("mitre_tactic")
    techniques = MITRE_TECHNIQUES.get(cat_id, [])

    return web.json_response({
        "category": {
            "id": cat_id,
            "label": cat_info["label"],
            "description": cat_info["description"],
            "color": cat_info["color"],
            "icon": cat_info["icon"],
            "mitre_tactic": mitre_tactic,
        },
        "stats": {
            "total": total,
            "unique_sources": len(sources),
            "unique_targets": len(targets),
            "affected_devices": len(device_alerts),
        },
        "severity_breakdown": sev_breakdown,
        "sub_categories": sub_list,
        "affected_devices": device_list,
        "top_signatures": signatures[:20],
        "mitre_techniques": techniques,
        "from": from_ts,
        "to": to_ts,
    })

docs.text:
Files: - Modify: daemon/api/alerts.py

Step 1: Add handler

async def handle_alert_category_timeline(request: web.Request) -> web.Response:
    """GET /api/alerts/categories/{category}/timeline — Time-series for one category."""
    cat_id = request.match_info["category"]
    client = _get_client(request)
    from_ts, to_ts = _parse_time_range(request)
    interval = request.query.get("interval", "1h")

    from services.alert_intelligence import THREAT_CATEGORIES, categorize_alert, categorize_sub_category

    if cat_id not in THREAT_CATEGORIES:
        return web.json_response({"error": f"Unknown category: {cat_id}"}, status=404)

    query = {
        "size": 0,
        "query": {"bool": {"filter": _suricata_alert_filters(from_ts, to_ts)}},
        "aggs": {
            "over_time": {
                "date_histogram": {"field": "@timestamp", "fixed_interval": interval, "min_doc_count": 0},
                "aggs": {
                    "by_signature": {"terms": {"field": "rule.name.keyword", "size": 200}},
                },
            },
        },
    }

    try:
        result = await _os_search(client, query)
    except Exception as exc:
        return web.json_response({"error": str(exc)}, status=502)

    time_buckets = result.get("aggregations", {}).get("over_time", {}).get("buckets", [])
    series = []

    for tb in time_buckets:
        point = {"timestamp": tb["key_as_string"], "total": 0, "sub_categories": {}}
        for sig_bucket in tb.get("by_signature", {}).get("buckets", []):
            sig = sig_bucket["key"]
            if categorize_alert(sig) != cat_id:
                continue
            count = sig_bucket["doc_count"]
            point["total"] += count
            sub_id = categorize_sub_category(sig, cat_id)
            if sub_id:
                point["sub_categories"][sub_id] = point["sub_categories"].get(sub_id, 0) + count
        series.append(point)

    return web.json_response({
        "category": cat_id, "from": from_ts, "to": to_ts,
        "interval": interval, "series": series,
    })

Step 2: Register route (in register_alert_routes):

export async function getEnhancedCategories(
  opts: TimeRangeParams = {}
): Promise<EnhancedCategoriesResponse> {
  const q = buildQuery(opts as Record<string, string | number | undefined>);
  const url = `/api/alerts/categories${q}`;
  try {
    const res = await fetch(url, { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(15_000) });
    if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`${res.status}`);
    return await res.json();
  } catch {
    return { from: '', to: '', categories: [] };
  }
}

    return await res.json();

    return {

      sub_categories: [], affected_devices: [], top_signatures: [], mitre_techniques: [],

export async function getCategoryTimeline(

docs.title: PCAP Collection Controls — Design Document
docs.text: Date: 2026-03-20 Status: Approved Branch: phase-4/pcap-controls

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Two features for PCAP collection management: 1. 100MB per-file cap — Each PCAP file rotates at 100MB (was 4096MB). User-configurable via Settings. 2. On/off toggle — Users can enable/disable PCAP collection. Stops/starts the nettap-pcap-capture container.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Per-file size cap defaults to 100MB, configurable (10–10000 MB)
  • Toggle stops the capture container; existing PCAPs remain accessible
  • Settings persist across reboots via /opt/nettap/data/.env
  • Quick toggle on PCAP page header; full config in Settings > Capture tab

docs.title: Backend: Capture Control API
docs.text:
New file: daemon/api/capture_control.py

Endpoint Method Body/Params Response /api/capture/status GET — {enabled, maxFileSizeMB, containerRunning, containerStatus} /api/capture/toggle PUT {enabled: bool} {enabled, containerRunning} /api/capture/settings PUT {maxFileSizeMB: number} {maxFileSizeMB, restarted}

docs.title: Toggle Mechanism
docs.text:
• ON: docker start nettap-pcap-capture
  • OFF: docker stop nettap-pcap-capture (graceful SIGTERM, container preserved)
  • Docker interaction via asyncio.create_subprocess_exec (no SDK dependency)

docs.title: Config Persistence
docs.text:
Two env vars in /opt/nettap/data/.env: - PCAP_CAPTURE_ENABLED=true|false (default: true) - PCAP_ROTATE_MB=100 (default: 100)

Reuses _load_env_file / _save_env_file from daemon/api/settings.py.

docs.title: Startup Behavior
docs.text: On daemon startup, read PCAP_CAPTURE_ENABLED. If false, stop the capture container. This ensures the setting survives reboots.

docs.title: File Size Change
docs.text: Updates PCAP_ROTATE_MB in env file. If capture is currently enabled, auto-restarts the container to apply (docker restart nettap-pcap-capture).

docs.title: Frontend: PCAP Page Toggle
docs.text:
Location: Top of /pcap page header.

  • Green dot + "Capture Active" / Red dot + "Capture Stopped" + toggle switch
  • Loading spinner during start/stop
  • On mount: GET /api/capture/status
  • Toggle: PUT /api/capture/toggle
  • Rest of PCAP page still works when capture is off (browse/search/download existing files)

docs.title: Frontend: Settings > Capture Tab
docs.text:
New tab in /settings between "Retention" and "API Keys".

Contents: 1. PCAP Collection toggle (synced with PCAP page) 2. Max File Size — number input, "MB" suffix, default 100, min 10, max 10000 3. Save button — PUT /api/capture/settings, auto-restarts container if size changed 4. Status card — container status, current file size, total PCAP disk usage

docs.title: Docker Compose Change
docs.text:
PCAP_ROTATE_MEGABYTES: "${PCAP_ROTATE_MB:-100}"  # was 4096

Default changes to 100MB for new deployments. Existing deployments with PCAP_ROTATE_MB in env keep their value.

For Claude: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task.

Goal: Add a 100MB per-file PCAP size cap (user-configurable) and an on/off toggle for PCAP capture that starts/stops the Docker container.

docs.title: Problem
docs.text: After implementing the bulletproof retention system, users have no visual confirmation that their retention settings are actually being enforced. The Settings/Retention tab lets you edit values but provides no feedback about system health — ILM policy sync, prune cycle activity, or disk pressure relative to thresholds.

docs.title: Solution
docs.text: Add a Retention Health status card at the top of the Settings/Retention tab with an overall health badge and 3 detail rows.

docs.title: Location
docs.text: Settings page > Retention tab > top of page, above the tier configuration cards.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
┌─ Retention Health ──────────────────────────┐
│                                              │
│  ● Healthy                                   │
│                                              │
│  ILM Policies    ✓ All 3 synced              │
│  Disk Usage      12.4% (threshold: 80%)      │
│  Last Prune      2 minutes ago               │
│                                              │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: Overall Status Logic
docs.text: Status Color Condition Healthy var(--success) ILM synced AND disk < 70% AND prune within 10 min Attention var(--warning) ILM pending retry OR disk 70-85% OR prune stale (>10 min) Problem var(--danger) ILM not synced (no retry) OR disk > emergency threshold

docs.title: Detail Rows
docs.text:
1. ILM Policies: Shows ✓ All 3 synced (green) or ⟳ Syncing... (yellow) or ✗ Out of sync (red)
  2. Disk Usage: Shows X.X% (threshold: Y%) with color based on proximity to threshold
  3. Last Prune: Shows relative time ("2 minutes ago"). Yellow if >10 min, red if >30 min or never

docs.title: IoT Trust Score Page — Design Document
docs.text: Date: 2026-04-04 Branch: phase-4/iot-trust-score Status: Approved

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
The current /iot page lists IoT devices by manufacturer, shows behavioral baselines (known destinations/ports/countries), and has a flat anomaly feed. It provides no actionable insight — a home user visiting this page can't quickly answer "is my smart home safe?"

Other pages already cover: device inventory (/devices), connections (/connections), IDS alerts (/alerts), kill chains (/threats), live traffic (/live), bandwidth (/bandwidth), DNS (/dns).

The white space is: per-device behavioral baselining, privacy/telemetry scoring, protocol compliance, encryption posture, lateral movement visibility, and manufacturer reputation — things that only make sense when analyzed per-device-class over time.

docs.title: Audience
docs.text: Home users who want plain-English, actionable answers. Not SOC analysts. Think: "credit score for your smart home."

docs.title: 1. Hero Score Card
docs.text:
Full-width card at the top: - Smart Home Health Score: Letter grade (A–F) + numeric 0–100 - Three sub-scores as colored badges: Privacy | Security | Behavior - Plain-English subtitle: "Your smart home is healthy. 1 device needs attention." - Score composite of all IoT devices' individual trust scores

Scoring formula (per device, 0–100): - Privacy (30 pts): tracker domains contacted, telemetry volume, third-party data sharing - Security (40 pts): encryption ratio, protocol compliance, alert count, firmware signals - Behavior (30 pts): baseline adherence, new destinations, volume spikes, unusual timing

Fleet score: Weighted average of device scores, with lowest-scoring device pulling the average down more heavily (harmonic mean approach).

docs.title: 2. Stat Cards Row
docs.text: 4 stat cards below the hero: | Card | Value | Color Logic | |------|-------|-------------| | IoT Devices | Total count | Always cyan | | Anomalies | Behavioral deviations (24h) | Green if 0, amber if 1–3, red if 4+ | | Privacy Concerns | Devices w/ privacy grade D or F | Green if 0, amber if 1–2, red if 3+ | | Unencrypted | Devices sending plaintext externally | Green if 0, red if any |

docs.title: 3. Device Trust Grid
docs.text: Grid of device cards sorted by risk (worst first): - Device name (UniFi alias > manufacturer > hostname > MAC) - Trust grade (A–F) with color badge: - A (90–100): green - B (75–89): cyan - C (60–74): amber - D (40–59): orange - F (0–39): red - Three mini indicators: Privacy grade, Encryption %, Anomaly count - Last seen timestamp - Click → opens device detail drawer

docs.title: 4. Manufacturer Profiles Section
docs.text: Card below device grid grouping devices by manufacturer: - Each manufacturer shows: device count, average trust score, avg privacy grade - Color-coded bar showing manufacturer "hygiene": - Encryption compliance (% of connections using TLS) - Tracker domain count across all devices from this manufacturer - Protocol violations count - Purpose: Helps users make purchasing decisions. "Ring devices on your network have a B+ security hygiene. TP-Link devices have a D." - Manufacturers sorted by worst hygiene first

docs.title: 5. Findings Feed
docs.text:
Chronological feed of noteworthy events: - Severity badge (Critical/High/Medium/Low) - Plain-English description: "Your Roku TV contacted 3 new tracking domains today" - Device name (clickable) - Timestamp + relative time ("3 hours ago") - Category tag pill: Privacy | Security | Behavior

Finding types: - Privacy: New tracker domains, telemetry volume spike, excessive phone-home - Security: Unencrypted external connection, unexpected protocol, beaconing, self-signed cert on WAN connection - Behavior: New destination not in baseline, new country, new port, unusual activity time, volume spike

docs.title: 6. Device Detail Drawer (on click)
docs.text:
5-tab drawer (480px, slides from right):

Tab 1 — Overview - Trust score breakdown (3 sub-scores with progress bars) - Device info: IP, MAC, manufacturer, hostname, first/last seen - Quick stats: daily data volume, connection count, unique destinations - Plain-English summary: "This device is behaving normally" or "This device has 2 findings"

Tab 2 — Communication Map - HorizontalBarList showing every destination, bars sized by bytes - Each row: hostname (or IP), country flag, bytes up/down - "In baseline" (green dot) or "NEW" (amber badge) per destination - Sort by: bytes, first seen, baseline status - Destinations outside baseline highlighted

Tab 3 — Privacy - Privacy grade (A–F) with explanation - Tracker domains contacted (HorizontalBarList, sorted by bytes) - Telemetry volume: bytes to trackers vs. functional domains (mini donut chart) - Phone-home frequency: connections per hour when device is "idle" - Encryption ratio: TLS vs plaintext (donut chart)

Tab 4 — Protocol Audit - Table: protocol/port | status (Expected / Unexpected) | connection count | last seen - Flags with plain-English explanations: - "Uses Telnet — this is an insecure remote access protocol" - "Bypasses your DNS — queries 8.8.8.8 directly instead of your router" - "Uses HTTP instead of HTTPS to send data externally"

Tab 5 — Activity Timeline - TimeSeriesChart: connection count per hour, 7-day window - Baseline overlay: shaded band showing "normal" activity hours and volume - Anomaly markers: red dots on the timeline where deviations occurred - Click a marker → shows the anomaly detail inline

docs.title: 7. Network Isolation Card (bottom of page)
docs.text: Card answering: "If a device were compromised, what could it reach?" - Table of IoT → non-IoT LAN communication pairs - Risk-sorted: - Critical: IoT → workstation (via SMB/CIFS) - High: IoT → NAS - Medium: IoT → other IoT - Info: IoT → router/gateway - Recommendation: "Consider creating a separate VLAN for your IoT devices — 3 IoT devices can currently reach your workstations"

docs.title: GET /api/iot/fleet-summary
docs.text: Returns overall health score, sub-scores, stat card data, devices-needing-attention list. Internally aggregates from other IoT services. Cached 60 seconds.

docs.title: GET /api/iot/privacy-report
docs.text: Per-device privacy grades (A–F) across 4 factors: - Tracker domains contacted (matched against daemon/data/tracker_domains.txt) - Telemetry volume (daily bytes uploaded) - Third-party data sharing (distinct destination orgs) - Encryption compliance (TLS vs plaintext ratio)

docs.title: GET /api/iot/devices/{mac}/communication-map
docs.text: Full destination map for a single device: - Each destination: IP, hostname (from DNS cross-query), country, port, bytes in/out, first/last seen - in_baseline: bool flag per destination - Sorted by bytes descending

docs.title: GET /api/iot/devices/{mac}/activity-timeline
docs.text: Hourly buckets over configurable window (default 7d): - Connection count, bytes sent/received, unique destinations, protocol breakdown - baseline_overlay: learned normal hours and average volumes

docs.title: GET /api/iot/protocol-audit
docs.text: Per-device protocol compliance check: - Expected protocols per device category (from daemon/data/protocol_profiles.json) - Actual protocols observed - Findings: unexpected protocols, unencrypted WAN connections, hardcoded DNS

docs.title: GET /api/iot/network-isolation
docs.text: Internal communication analysis: - IoT devices that communicated with non-IoT LAN devices - Risk classification per pairing - Segmentation score (0–100)

docs.title: GET /api/iot/manufacturer-profiles
docs.text: Aggregated manufacturer statistics: - Device count per manufacturer - Average trust score, privacy grade - Encryption compliance %, tracker domain count, protocol violations

docs.title: Data Files Required
docs.text:
• daemon/data/tracker_domains.txt — ~200 known analytics/tracking domains (crashlytics.com, mixpanel.com, amplitude.com, doubleclick.net, etc.)
  • daemon/data/protocol_profiles.json — Expected port/protocol sets per IoT device category (camera, thermostat, smart speaker, hub, TV, plug, etc.)

docs.title: Design System Compliance
docs.text:
• All colors via CSS variables (var(--green), var(--danger), etc.)
  • All spacing via spacing vars (var(--space-md))
  • All text via text vars (var(--text-sm))
  • No max-width on page container
  • All tables sortable
  • Use existing components: HorizontalBarList, DetailDrawer, DrawerSection, KVRow, TimeSeriesChart, DonutChart, stat cards, pills, badges
  • Monospace for IPs, MACs, ports
  • Responsive: 2-col grid at 1024px, 1-col at 768px

docs.title: What This Page Does NOT Do (Avoid Overlap)
docs.text:
• General device inventory → /devices
  • All connection logs → /connections
  • IDS/Suricata alerts → /alerts
  • Kill chain / threat intel → /threats
  • Bandwidth monitoring → /bandwidth
  • DNS query logs → /dns
  • Live traffic → /live

The IoT page cross-references these (e.g., "3 alerts for this device — view on Alerts page") but does not duplicate them.

docs.title: Verification Plan
docs.text:
1. Backend: cd daemon && python -m pytest — all tests pass
  2. Frontend: cd web && npx vitest run — all tests pass
  3. Type check: cd web && npx svelte-check — no errors
  4. Manual: Load /iot page with IoT devices on the network, verify:
  5. Hero score renders with letter grade
  6. Device cards sorted by risk
  7. Click device → drawer opens with 5 tabs
  8. Privacy tab shows tracker domains
  9. Communication map shows baseline comparison
  10. Network isolation card shows LAN pairs
  11. Manufacturer profiles show aggregated data

docs.title: IoT Trust Score Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For Claude: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task.

Goal: Replace the basic IoT page with an IoT Trust Score dashboard that gives home users a "credit score for your smart home" — combining security scoring, privacy monitoring, and behavioral change detection.

Architecture: Backend adds 7 new endpoints to the existing aiohttp daemon, extending the IoTMonitor service and adding new service classes. Two static data files (tracker domains, protocol profiles) power the privacy and protocol audit features. Frontend replaces the existing /iot/+page.svelte with a new page using existing components (HorizontalBarList, DetailDrawer, TimeSeriesChart, DonutChart). The catch-all proxy at web/src/routes/api/[...path]/+server.ts handles all /api/iot/* routing.

Tech Stack: Python/aiohttp (backend), Svelte 5 with runes (frontend), OpenSearch query DSL, pure SVG charts

Design doc: docs/plans/2026-04-04-iot-trust-score-design.md

"""IoT Trust Score computation.

Computes per-device trust scores (0-100) across three pillars:
- Privacy (30 pts): tracker domains, telemetry volume, third-party sharing
- Security (40 pts): encryption ratio, protocol compliance, alerts, firmware
- Behavior (30 pts): baseline adherence, new destinations, volume spikes, timing
"""

import logging

logger = logging.getLogger("nettap.services.iot_trust_scorer")


class IoTTrustScorer:
    """Computes IoT device trust scores."""

    # --- Privacy weights (30 pts total) ---
    _PRIV_TRACKERS_MAX = 10        # 0 trackers = 10, 20+ = 0
    _PRIV_TELEMETRY_MAX = 10       # Low volume = 10, high = 0
    _PRIV_THIRD_PARTY_MAX = 10     # 1 org = 10, 10+ = 0

    # --- Security weights (40 pts total) ---
    _SEC_ENCRYPTION_MAX = 15       # 100% TLS = 15, 0% = 0
    _SEC_PROTOCOL_MAX = 10         # 0 violations = 10
    _SEC_ALERTS_MAX = 10           # 0 alerts = 10
    _SEC_FIRMWARE_MAX = 5          # Current = 5, stale = 0

    # --- Behavior weights (30 pts total) ---
    _BEH_BASELINE_MAX = 15         # 100% adherence = 15
    _BEH_NEW_DEST_MAX = 5          # 0 new = 5
    _BEH_VOLUME_MAX = 5            # No spike = 5
    _BEH_TIMING_MAX = 5            # Normal hours = 5

    def score_device(self, stats: dict) -> dict:
        """Score a single device. Returns score, grade, and sub-scores."""
        privacy = self._score_privacy(stats)
        security = self._score_security(stats)
        behavior = self._score_behavior(stats)

        total = privacy + security + behavior
        grade = self.score_to_grade(total)

        return {
            "score": total,
            "grade": grade,
            "privacy_score": round(privacy * 100 / 30),
            "security_score": round(security * 100 / 40),
            "behavior_score": round(behavior * 100 / 30),
            "privacy_raw": round(privacy, 1),
            "security_raw": round(security, 1),
            "behavior_raw": round(behavior, 1),
        }

    def _score_privacy(self, stats: dict) -> float:
        trackers = stats.get("tracker_domain_count", 0)
        telem = stats.get("telemetry_bytes", 0)
        orgs = stats.get("third_party_orgs", 1)

        t_score = max(0, self._PRIV_TRACKERS_MAX - trackers * 0.5)
        v_score = self._PRIV_TELEMETRY_MAX * max(0, 1 - telem / 100_000_000)
        o_score = max(0, self._PRIV_THIRD_PARTY_MAX - (orgs - 1) * 1.0)

        return min(30, t_score + v_score + o_score)

    def _score_security(self, stats: dict) -> float:
        enc_ratio = stats.get("encryption_ratio", 1.0)
        violations = stats.get("protocol_violations", 0)
        alerts = stats.get("alert_count", 0)
        firmware = stats.get("firmware_age_signal", "unknown")

        e_score = self._SEC_ENCRYPTION_MAX * enc_ratio
        p_score = max(0, self._SEC_PROTOCOL_MAX - violations * 3)
        a_score = max(0, self._SEC_ALERTS_MAX - alerts * 2)
        f_score = {"current": 5, "recent": 3, "unknown": 2, "stale": 0}.get(firmware, 2)

        return min(40, e_score + p_score + a_score + f_score)

    def _score_behavior(self, stats: dict) -> float:
        adherence = stats.get("baseline_adherence", 1.0)
        new_dest = stats.get("new_destinations", 0)
        spike = stats.get("volume_spike", False)
        timing = stats.get("unusual_timing", False)

        b_score = self._BEH_BASELINE_MAX * adherence
        d_score = max(0, self._BEH_NEW_DEST_MAX - new_dest)
        v_score = 0 if spike else self._BEH_VOLUME_MAX
        t_score = 0 if timing else self._BEH_TIMING_MAX

        return min(30, b_score + d_score + v_score + t_score)

    @staticmethod
    def score_to_grade(score: int) -> str:
        if score >= 90:
            return "A"
        if score >= 75:
            return "B"
        if score >= 60:
            return "C"
        if score >= 40:
            return "D"
        return "F"

    @staticmethod
    def compute_fleet_score(device_scores: list[int]) -> int:
        """Harmonic mean — one bad device tanks the fleet score."""
        if not device_scores:
            return 100
        # Avoid division by zero: treat 0-score devices as 1
        safe = [max(s, 1) for s in device_scores]
        harmonic = len(safe) / sum(1.0 / s for s in safe)
        return round(harmonic)

docs.title: DHCP Gateway Capture Mode — Design
docs.text: Date: 2026-10-30 Status: Approved for implementation (owner decisions locked 2026-10-30) Branch: phase-4/dhcp-gateway-mode (stacked on fix/pr110-review, PR #144) Related: Debugging/BRIDGE-ARCHITECTURE.md, memory dhcp-gateway-mode

docs.title: 1. Why
docs.text:
The inline bridge sits between the ISP modem and the router, so it only sees traffic after the router's NAT. Every device shows up as the router's public IP, so NetTap can't answer "what is each of my devices doing?".

DHCP gateway mode puts NetTap in front of the router's NAT. NetTap hands out addresses, names itself as the gateway, and routes traffic on to the real router. Every flow then carries the device's real IP and MAC. It works on any router and needs no managed switch. Firewalla's DHCP mode works the same way.

docs.title: 2. Owner decisions (locked)
docs.text: Decision Choice Onboarding modes DHCP gateway (recommended) and Mirror port are primary. The inline bridge stays under "Advanced". No bridge code is removed. One-way traffic fix NetTap serves its own subnet (default 10.77.0.0/24) and masquerades to the router (double NAT). The only router change: turn off the router's DHCP. Review findings Listed only. Code that this work rewrites must not carry a finding forward.

docs.title: 3. Topology (one-armed)
docs.text:
ISP modem
                      │
              ┌───────┴────────┐
              │  Home router   │  192.168.1.1/24  (DHCP OFF)
              └───────┬────────┘
                      │ LAN port / switch / router Wi-Fi
     ┌────────────────┼──────────────────────────┐
     │                │                          │
  NetTap LAN NIC   phone, TV, laptop ...      static-IP devices
  192.168.1.50/24  10.77.0.x/24                (bypass NetTap)
  10.77.0.1/24     gw = 10.77.0.1
                   dns = 192.168.1.1
  • One NIC (the one plugged into the router) carries both legs: device ↔ NetTap (10.77.0.x, pre-NAT) and NetTap ↔ router (192.168.1.50, post-NAT). A 2.5GbE port gives each direction plenty of headroom for a WAN of 1 Gbps or less.
  • Devices on Wi-Fi from the router's own access point are covered too, because DHCP and the gateway are L3, not tied to a cable.
  • NetTap keeps its existing address on the router subnet (192.168.1.50 above), so the dashboard URL does not change. That address becomes static, because nothing will renew it once the router's DHCP is off.

docs.title: 4.1 DHCP server: dnsmasq, run by the daemon
docs.text:
• dnsmasq-base is added to the daemon image. The daemon already runs with network_mode: host, NET_ADMIN and NET_RAW. Add NET_BIND_SERVICE (UDP 67), SETUID and SETGID (dnsmasq drops to nobody:nogroup) and KILL (the root daemon can only signal the nobody-owned dnsmasq with it) to its cap_add.
  • DHCP only: --port=0 disables DNS. NetTap is not a DNS server. Option 6 (DNS) hands out the router's IP. DNS queries still pass through NetTap as the gateway, so Zeek's dns.log attributes them to the real device. This also means a daemon restart never breaks name resolution.
  • Arguments (no config file): --keep-in-foreground --port=0 --conf-file=/dev/null --pid-file --user=nobody --group=nogroup --interface=<lan> --except-interface=lo --bind-interfaces --dhcp-authoritative --dhcp-range=<pool_start>,<pool_end>,<netmask>,1h --dhcp-option=option:router,<gateway_ip> --dhcp-option=option:dns-server,<upstream_gateway> --dhcp-leasefile=/var/lib/nettap/dhcp/dnsmasq.leases --log-facility=-. dnsmasq must not run as root: it opens its sockets and the lease file as root, then drops to nobody:nogroup (uid/gid 65534 in the python:3.12-slim-bookworm image), keeping only NET_ADMIN and NET_RAW. The lease file stays root-owned: root in the container has no DAC_OVERRIDE, so a nobody-owned file would stop dnsmasq opening it. The already-open file is still written after the drop. --pid-file with no value writes no pid file (the daemon supervises the child; as nobody, dnsmasq can't chown one in /var/run). Verified in the image with cap_drop: ALL and exactly the capabilities above: a client got a lease and it was written to the file.
  • Pool: host offsets 10 … last-host (10.77.0.10–10.77.0.254 for a /24). .1 is the gateway, .2–.9 are left for the user's static assignments.
  • Lease time: 1 hour. Rollback (router DHCP back on, NetTap DHCP off) completes within one lease at worst. Renewals every 30 min per device are negligible traffic. A daemon outage shorter than a lease is invisible to clients.
  • The lease file lives on the storage-data volume (/var/lib/nettap), so it survives restarts.
  • The daemon supervises the child: reconcile() restarts it if it exited.

docs.title: 4.2 Routing and NAT
docs.text:
Runtime (daemon, host network namespace, existing nsenter -t 1 -n pattern):

  1. ip addr add <gateway_ip>/<prefix> dev <lan>, if missing.
  2. Re-assert the upstream address and default route if missing (see §4.4).
  3. Firewall rules, all tagged -m comment --comment nettap-dhcp-gateway and added only after a -C check (idempotent):
  4. filter DOCKER-USER -i <lan> -o <lan> -s <subnet> -j ACCEPT
  5. filter DOCKER-USER -i <lan> -o <lan> -d <subnet> -m conntrack --ctstate RELATED,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT

Both are pinned to -i <lan> -o <lan> (the one-armed path). Without -o, the accept would end FORWARD before Docker's own chains run, and every LAN device could reach unpublished container ports (Redis, OpenSearch) on the Docker bridges. Published ports (nginx 80/443) still work through Docker's DNAT rules. All rules are inserted with -I. - nat POSTROUTING -o <lan> -s <subnet> ! -d <subnet> -j MASQUERADE - filter OUTPUT -o <lan> -p icmp --icmp-type redirect -j DROP 4. ethtool -K <lan> gro off lro off (accurate capture; failure is only a warning).

Why DOCKER-USER: Docker sets the FORWARD policy to DROP. An accept rule in our own nft table doesn't help, because every base chain on the hook must accept. DOCKER-USER is the chain Docker documents for user rules. It is jumped to first and Docker never flushes it.

Why drop ICMP redirects: in-interface == out-interface on a one-armed router, so Linux would send redirects telling devices to go straight to the router. /proc/sys is read-only inside the container, so the runtime fix is the OUTPUT drop rule. send_redirects=0 is persisted for boot (§4.5).

Firewall backend detection: iptables is added to the daemon image (Debian ships both iptables-nft and iptables-legacy). Use whichever backend has a DOCKER-USER chain (<cmd> -w -S DOCKER-USER exits 0), trying nft first. If neither has one, the backend is null, which is a blocking preflight failure. That is conservative: we never guess which table Docker's DROP policy lives in.

IP forwarding: Docker already sets net.ipv4.ip_forward=1. Preflight reads /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_forward. 0 is a blocking failure, because the container can't write /proc/sys.

docs.title: 4.3 Capture: device leg only, exactly once
docs.text:
Each routed flow crosses the LAN NIC twice: the device leg and the post-NAT router leg. Capture is limited to the device leg with a BPF filter:

PCAP_FILTER = "net <subnet> or udp port 67 or udp port 68"

DHCP broadcasts (src 0.0.0.0) are kept for Zeek's dhcp.log (hostname ↔ MAC ↔ IP).

Confirmed against the Malcolm v26.02.0 source:

Tool Reads the filter from Notes Arkime PCAP_FILTER → bpf= in config.ini (arkime/scripts/docker_entrypoint.sh:132) works Suricata CAPTURE_FILTER/PCAP_FILTER → af-packet bpf-filter (suricata_config_populate.py:883-892) works netsniff-ng (pcap-capture) PCAP_FILTER works Zeek zeekdeploy.sh exports CAPTURE_FILTER from PCAP_FILTER; Malcolm's local.zeek turns it into restrict_filters (getenv("CAPTURE_FILTER"), the fix for Malcolm issue #474, now closed) works. The review (CR-091) found that NetTap's config/zeek/nettap.zeek mount targets /opt/zeek/... while the image installs Zeek to /usr/local/zeek, so Malcolm's own local.zeek, with its filter hook, is what runs. Do not touch nettap.zeek in this work. CR-091 tracks the dead mount.

Getting the interface and filter to the capture containers. Today PCAP_IFACE comes only from compose interpolation (docker/.env), which the daemon can't write. That is why the wizard's mirror choice never takes effect (the "capture settings have no effect" follow-up from PR #144). Fix:

  • Bind-mount the host directory /etc/nettap: read-write into the daemon at /etc/nettap, read-only into zeek-live, suricata-live, arkime-live and pcap-capture. That is the default path capture_config.py already uses for capture-mode.conf and capture.env.
  • config/capture/nettap-capture-env.sh (mounted read-only into each capture container) parses /etc/nettap/capture.env without sourcing it. It exports only PCAP_IFACE, PCAP_FILTER and CAPTURE_FILTER (same value as PCAP_FILTER), and only when the file exists. Each capture entrypoint wrapper runs . /usr/local/bin/nettap-capture-env.sh before exec tini. When the file is missing, the compose env stays in effect, so existing installs are unchanged.
  • The daemon writes capture.env atomically (temp file + rename) and restarts the four capture containers through the existing capture_control._docker_cmd helper (docker CLI over the socket the daemon already mounts). A restart re-runs the entrypoint, which re-reads the file. Containers are never created or removed.
  • Values are validated before they are written: interface ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,15}$; the subnet is parsed with ipaddress; the filter is built only from the validated subnet.

docs.title: 4.4 NetTap's own address (the router DHCP is about to go away)
docs.text:
Once the router's DHCP is off, systemd-networkd can't renew NetTap's lease. When the lease expires it removes the address and the DHCP default route, and NetTap stops routing. The daemon can't run netplan apply (no host mount namespace, no D-Bus), so:

  1. On enable, record the current upstream address (192.168.1.50/24) and gateway (192.168.1.1) in capture-mode.conf.
  2. Persist for boot: /etc/netplan/90-nettap-dhcp-gateway.yaml (mode 0600) sets the LAN NIC to dhcp4: false, with addresses [upstream, gateway_ip/prefix], a default route via the upstream gateway, and the upstream gateway as nameserver.
  3. Self-heal at runtime: reconcile() runs every capture-health interval (30 s). It re-adds the upstream address and the default route if networkd removed them, re-adds the gateway address and firewall rules, and restarts dnsmasq if it died. If networkd drops the address when the old lease expires, routing blips for at most one interval.
  4. Recommended: reboot NetTap once after activation. Netplan then applies, networkd stops running DHCP on the LAN NIC, and the blip can't happen. The go-live page says so. NetTap's own outbound DNS (feeds, GeoIP updates) may fail between lease expiry and that reboot. Clients are unaffected, because they use the router for DNS directly. Caveat (review CR-025): installs that use nettap.service run docker compose down on stop, so a reboot recreates OpenSearch and its security mapping reverts. Until CR-025 is fixed, run the OpenSearch security bootstrap from CLAUDE.md after any reboot. The go-live copy links to it.

docs.title: 4.5 Boot persistence (no dependency on the daemon starting)
docs.text:
The daemon only starts after OpenSearch is healthy, which can take minutes on an N100. Routing must come back before that:

File (host path) Purpose /etc/netplan/90-nettap-dhcp-gateway.yaml static upstream address, gateway address, default route /etc/sysctl.d/99-nettap-dhcp-gateway.conf ip_forward=1, send_redirects=0 (all, default, <lan>) /etc/nettap/dhcp-gateway-firewall.sh (0755) idempotent host-iptables rules (same rule list as runtime). Waits up to 60 s for DOCKER-USER /etc/systemd/system/nettap-dhcp-gateway.service oneshot, After=docker.service, runs the script. Enabled via a symlink in multi-user.target.wants whose target is the host path /etc/systemd/system/nettap-dhcp-gateway.service

The host's own iptables uses the same backend as the host's Docker, so the boot script needs no backend detection. dnsmasq starts with the daemon, a few minutes after boot. Clients renewing mid-lease don't notice. New devices wait until the daemon is up.

Existing bug noted for the review table as LD-001 (not fixed here): BridgeManager and MirrorManager create their multi-user.target.wants symlinks with the container path (/host/etc/systemd/system/...) as the target. On the host those symlinks dangle, so their units are never enabled. The DHCP unit uses the host path.

docs.title: 4.5.1 Review findings this work must not carry forward
docs.text:
These sit in code this feature rewrites, so the rewrite fixes them. Commits cite the IDs.

ID What the rewrite does CR-007 The wizard's mode and NIC choice reach load_capture_config (INI at /etc/nettap/capture-mode.conf) and the capture containers (capture.env + restart) CR-165, CR-166 /api/setup/configure validates interface names (^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,15}$) and the DHCP subnet before writing anything CR-167 main.py starts the storage and SMART loops before capture setup, and wraps capture config load and manager setup in try/except with a logged fallback, so a bad capture-mode.conf can't crash-loop the daemon CR-212, CR-247 CaptureHealthPanel and the Infrastructure page label dhcp_gateway correctly instead of showing bridge/br0

Related findings not fixed here, but relevant to operators of this mode: CR-075 (the rogue-DHCP detector flags clients; nothing consumes it yet), CR-025 (reboot recreates OpenSearch), CR-091 (dead nettap.zeek mount), CR-114 (the capture-mode store loads once per session).

docs.title: 4.6 Safety
docs.text: Risk Mitigation Two DHCP servers on one LAN Preflight sends a real DHCPDISCOVER (AF_PACKET, broadcast flag, 3 s listen) and lists every server that answers. Enable is refused (409) while any server other than NetTap answers, and the probe runs again inside enable. dnsmasq is never started without a probe, at daemon start and in reconcile() alike. If another server answers, the DHCP setting is saved as off and the issue is shown. If the probe errors, NetTap holds DHCP off for that tick only and probes again on the next one, because the router's DHCP is off by design. Leaving an active gateway in the wizard is refused (409) until another DHCP server answers. Subnet collides with an existing network Checked against every IPv4 network on every host interface (router subnet, docker0, br-*). Blocking. NetTap down ⇒ no internet Stated plainly before enabling (explicit confirmation). Kernel forwarding and NAT survive daemon crashes. The boot unit restores routing without the daemon. The recovery steps are shown on the go-live page and in this doc (§7). IPv6 bypass If the router advertises IPv6 (RA), devices get global IPv6 and the router as their v6 gateway, so that traffic bypasses NetTap. Detected from a proto ra default route or a dynamic global address on the LAN NIC. Warning, not blocking, with advice to turn off IPv6 on the router for full visibility. Static-IP devices / mesh routers that can't disable DHCP Wizard and go-live copy. If the router can't turn DHCP off, the re-probe keeps failing and the UI recommends Mirror or the Advanced bridge. Double NAT Documented: router port forwards and UPnP don't reach devices, and consoles may report strict NAT. A NetTap-side port-forward UI is a follow-up. Device-to-device LAN traffic Devices on 10.77.0.0/24 share L2 and talk directly, so that traffic stays invisible (needs Mirror).

docs.title: 4.7 Latency and throughput
docs.text: The extra L3 hop costs tens of µs (typical, unmeasured), the same order as the bridge and well under the 1 ms budget. The real risk is jitter while Zeek/Suricata/Arkime saturate the N100. The remote script measures host→router and host→1.1.1.1 RTT with capture running, and prints the iperf3 command to run from a client for throughput. This can't be verified from the dev machine.

docs.title: 5. State and config
docs.text:
/etc/nettap/capture-mode.conf (INI, read by load_capture_config, written by save_capture_config):

[capture]
mode = dhcp_gateway
interface = enp1s0
management =

[bridge]
wan_interface = eth0
lan_interface = eth1

[dhcp_gateway]
subnet = 10.77.0.0/24
upstream_address = 192.168.1.50/24     ; set by enable, empty until then
upstream_gateway = 192.168.1.1         ; set by enable, empty until then
dhcp_enabled = false                   ; DHCP server on/off
  • Routing active ⇔ mode == dhcp_gateway and upstream_gateway set.
  • DHCP server running ⇔ routing active and dhcp_enabled.
  • disable turns off only the DHCP server. Routing stays, so devices holding 10.77.0.x leases keep working until they move back to the router (within one lease, or on reconnect).
  • Switching to another mode in the wizard calls teardown(): stop dnsmasq, delete the rules, remove the gateway address, delete the four boot files. The UI warns to turn the router's DHCP back on before rebooting NetTap.

/etc/nettap/capture.env (consumed by capture containers):

CAPTURE_MODE=dhcp_gateway
PCAP_IFACE=enp1s0
PCAP_FILTER=net 10.77.0.0/24 or udp port 67 or udp port 68

(mirror: PCAP_IFACE=<mirror nic>, PCAP_FILTER=; bridge: PCAP_IFACE=br0, PCAP_FILTER=.)

docs.title: 6.1 Daemon modules
docs.text: File Contents daemon/services/capture_manager.py CaptureMode.DHCP_GATEWAY = "dhcp_gateway"; non-abstract async def reconcile(self) -> None (default no-op) daemon/services/capture_config.py CaptureConfig gains dhcp_subnet="10.77.0.0/24", dhcp_upstream_address="", dhcp_upstream_gateway="", dhcp_enabled=False; [dhcp_gateway] read/write; write_env_file emits PCAP_FILTER; atomic writes daemon/services/dhcp_probe.py build_discover(xid: int, mac: bytes) -> bytes; parse_offer(frame: bytes, xid: int) -> dict \| None ({"server_ip", "offered_ip"}); async probe_dhcp_servers(iface: str, mac: str, timeout: float = 3.0) -> list[dict] daemon/services/dhcp_gateway_net.py Pure helpers: validate_subnet, gateway_ip, pool_range, capture_filter, firewall_rules(subnet, iface), render_netplan(...), render_sysctl(iface), render_firewall_script(...), render_systemd_unit(), parse_leases(text) daemon/services/dhcp_gateway.py DhcpGatewayManager(CaptureManager): setup, teardown, get_health, get_capture_interface, get_stats, mode, reconcile, plus preflight(), enable(), disable(), status() daemon/api/dhcp_gateway.py Routes below; register_dhcp_gateway_routes(app) called from server.py daemon/api/setup.py Accepts capture_mode: "dhcp_gateway"; writes INI + capture.env to the paths the readers use; restarts capture containers when capture.env changes; swaps app["capture_manager"] (tearing down an active DHCP gateway first) daemon/main.py DHCP branch at startup (calls setup() if routing active). The generic capture loop reads app["capture_manager"] each tick and calls reconcile() then get_health(), and runs in every mode. Storage and SMART tasks start before capture setup, and capture setup is guarded (CR-167)

docs.title: 6.2 HTTP API (daemon; session required. preflight and status go through the web catch-all proxy; enable, disable and /api/setup/configure have dedicated SvelteKit routes with a 60 s timeout, because enable probes for 3 s, waits for dnsmasq and may restart the capture containers)
docs.text:
All four return 409 {"error": ...} when the configured mode isn't dhcp_gateway.

GET /api/capture/dhcp/preflight → 200

{
  "interface": "enp1s0",
  "subnet": "10.77.0.0/24",
  "gateway_ip": "10.77.0.1",
  "upstream": {"address": "192.168.1.50/24", "gateway": "192.168.1.1"},
  "subnet_conflicts": [],
  "other_dhcp_servers": [{"server_ip": "192.168.1.1", "offered_ip": "192.168.1.77"}],
  "ipv6_router_advertisements": true,
  "ip_forward": true,
  "firewall_backend": "iptables-nft",
  "checks": [{"name": "no_other_dhcp", "passed": false, "blocking": true,
              "message": "Your router's DHCP server is still on (192.168.1.1)."}],
  "ready": false
}

upstream is null when the NIC has no router-subnet address or default route. Check names: interface_up, upstream_detected, no_other_dhcp, no_subnet_conflict, ip_forward, firewall_backend (all blocking) and ipv6_bypass (non-blocking). ready = every blocking check passed.

POST /api/capture/dhcp/enable, body {"confirm": true} → 200 status body (below). 400 without confirm: true. 409 {"error", "checks"} when a fresh preflight fails a blocking check. 500 {"error"} when applying fails (partial state is rolled back).

POST /api/capture/dhcp/disable → 200 status body.

GET /api/capture/dhcp/status → 200

{
  "interface": "enp1s0",
  "subnet": "10.77.0.0/24",
  "gateway_ip": "10.77.0.1",
  "upstream": {"address": "192.168.1.50/24", "gateway": "192.168.1.1"},
  "routing_active": true,
  "dhcp_enabled": true,
  "dhcp_server_running": true,
  "leases": [{"mac": "aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff", "ip": "10.77.0.23", "hostname": "pixel-8", "expires": 1793389200}],
  "issues": []
}

POST /api/setup/configure (existing) adds: {"capture_mode": "dhcp_gateway", "capture_interface": "enp1s0", "dhcp_subnet": "10.77.0.0/24"}. dhcp_subnet is optional (defaults to 10.77.0.0/24) and validated as private, prefix 16–28. The response adds "capture_restart": {"restarted": [...], "errors": [...]}.

GET /api/capture/health in DHCP mode: mode: "dhcp_gateway", status is not_configured (not enabled yet), normal, degraded or down, plus extra keys subnet, routing_active, dhcp_server_running, lease_count.

docs.title: 6.3 Web
docs.text: File Contents web/src/lib/api/dhcpGateway.ts Types mirroring §6.2; getDhcpPreflight, enableDhcpGateway, disableDhcpGateway, getDhcpStatus (throw Error(message) on non-OK, with the daemon's error text) web/src/lib/utils/dhcpSubnet.ts validateDhcpSubnet(cidr, nicAddresses) -> { valid: boolean; error: string } (format, private range, prefix 16–28, not containing any NIC address) web/src/lib/components/setup/DhcpGatewayStep.svelte Wizard step: subnet input (bindable), validation, what happens / limitations in plain English web/src/routes/setup/+page.svelte Mode cards: DHCP gateway (Recommended), Mirror/SPAN. Inline bridge inside an "Advanced" Collapsible. DHCP steps: Welcome → Capture Mode → Interfaces (one NIC, "plugged into your router") → DHCP Gateway → Storage → Enrichment → Account → Verification web/src/lib/components/golive/DhcpGoLive.svelte Preflight checks → guided "turn off your router's DHCP" + re-check → confirmation checkbox → Enable → live status (sortable lease table, issues) → Disable + recovery steps web/src/routes/go-live/+page.svelte Reads /api/capture/mode. dhcp_gateway renders DhcpGoLive, anything else the existing bridge flow (bridge polling starts only in bridge mode) web/src/lib/stores/captureMode.ts Store type adds 'dhcp_gateway'

docs.title: 7. Recovery (shown on the go-live page)
docs.text:
If NetTap is off or broken and devices have no internet:

  1. Turn the router's DHCP server back on. With NetTap down and the router's DHCP off, nothing hands out addresses, so the user first gives a laptop a fixed address on the router's network (plugged into the router or on its Wi-Fi). When status.upstream is known the page fills in real values: a free host in the router's network (host .20, skipping NetTap and the router), the netmask from the upstream prefix, and the router address, e.g. "IP 192.168.1.20, mask 255.255.255.0, then open http://192.168.1.1" (staticAddressHint in web/src/lib/utils/dhcpSubnet.ts). Without upstream it says to pick a free address in the router's range and find the router's address on its sticker. Routers managed with a phone app (most mesh systems) are switched back in the app instead, on mobile data if the Wi-Fi has no internet.
  2. Reconnect devices (Wi-Fi off/on, or unplug and replug) and they get router addresses straight away; otherwise they move over when their NetTap address runs out (lease time 1 h). Set the laptop back to automatic addressing.
  3. Once NetTap is healthy again, switch the DHCP gateway back on from Go Live.

Timing copy for the switch to NetTap: devices move over when their current address from the router runs out (often up to a day), or straight away if they reconnect (Wi-Fi off/on or replug). Never promise a fixed number of minutes.

Mode changes: the setup wizard can't save after first run, so no copy sends users to Setup to switch modes or pick a new subnet. Where a router can't turn its DHCP off, the page says switching modes after setup isn't available in the app yet.

docs.title: 8. Tests
docs.text:
• pytest: probe packet build/parse (fixtures), subnet/pool/filter helpers, firewall rule list, renderers (netplan/sysctl/script/unit content, host-path symlink), lease parsing, backend detection, enable refusal paths (other DHCP, conflict, no upstream, no backend, no confirm), rollback on apply failure, reconcile re-adds missing pieces, disable keeps routing, teardown removes everything, configure writes INI + capture.env at the reader paths, container restart only on change, 409 on mode mismatch.
  • vitest: API client (URLs, methods, errors), subnet validator, wizard (DHCP and Mirror primary, bridge under Advanced, DHCP step flow, payload), DhcpGoLive (loading/error/blocked/ready/enabled states, enable needs the confirmation, sortable lease table, disable), go-live mode switch, store.

docs.title: 9. Out of scope / follow-ups
docs.text:
• NetTap-side port forwarding (double-NAT workaround).
  • In-app host reboot or netplan apply (would need a new host privilege path).
  • IPv6 routing through NetTap (RA suppression or NAT66).
  • DHCP reservations UI; importing the router's existing reservations.

docs.title: CLI Reference
docs.text: Complete reference for all NetTap shell scripts and their options.

docs.title: scripts/install/install.sh
docs.text:
Main installation script. Orchestrates the full deployment: pre-flight checks, system dependencies, network bridge, Malcolm stack, systemd services, mDNS, and verification.

sudo scripts/install/install.sh [OPTIONS]
Option Description --skip-bridge Skip bridge configuration (if already done) --skip-pull Skip Docker image pull (use cached images) --skip-malcolm Skip Malcolm deployment entirely (bridge + deps only) --no-persist-bridge Don't write persistent netplan config (runtime-only bridge) --dry-run Log all actions without executing them -v, --verbose Enable debug output -h, --help Show help

Steps executed:

  1. Pre-flight checks (root, OS, architecture, hardware validation)
  2. System dependencies (Docker, bridge-utils, net-tools, Python, Avahi)
  3. Kernel tuning (vm.max_map_count, network buffers, conntrack)
  4. Network bridge (br0 with WAN + LAN NICs)
  5. Malcolm deployment (container images, TLS certs, auth)
  6. Systemd services (nettap.service)
  7. mDNS configuration (Avahi)
  8. Firewall rules (UFW, if active)
  9. Post-install verification

docs.title: scripts/install/validate-hardware.sh
docs.text:
Hardware validation. Checks CPU, RAM, disk, and NIC count against minimum requirements.

Can be sourced (provides validate_hardware function) or run standalone:

sudo scripts/install/validate-hardware.sh

Exit codes:

Code Meaning 0 All checks passed 1 Warnings (e.g., below recommended but above minimum) 2 Hard failure (does not meet minimum requirements)

Thresholds:

Check Minimum Recommended CPU cores 2 4 RAM 8 GB (~7500 MB) 16 GB (~15000 MB) Disk 512 GB (~400 GB formatted) 1 TB NICs 2 physical 3 (including management)

docs.title: scripts/bridge/setup-bridge.sh
docs.text:
Create, validate, or tear down the transparent network bridge.

sudo scripts/bridge/setup-bridge.sh [OPTIONS]
Option Description --wan <iface> WAN-side interface (default: $WAN_INTERFACE or eth0) --lan <iface> LAN-side interface (default: $LAN_INTERFACE or eth1) --mgmt <iface> Management interface for dashboard access --persist Write netplan config and systemd units for boot persistence --no-persist Skip persistence (runtime only, for testing) --validate-only Check existing bridge config without making changes --teardown Remove bridge and restore interfaces to original state --detect Auto-detect NICs and suggest WAN/LAN assignment --dry-run Log commands without executing -v, --verbose Debug output -h, --help Show help

Modes:

Create (default)ValidateTeardownDetect 
sudo scripts/bridge/setup-bridge.sh --wan eth0 --lan eth1 --persist

Creates br0, adds NICs, tunes offloads, enables promiscuous mode, and optionally writes netplan config for persistence.

sudo scripts/bridge/setup-bridge.sh --validate-only

Checks bridge exists, is UP, STP disabled, interfaces attached, promiscuous mode on, forward delay 0.

sudo scripts/bridge/setup-bridge.sh --teardown

Removes bridge, restores interfaces, cleans up netplan config, systemd units, and sysctl settings.

scripts/bridge/setup-bridge.sh --detect

Lists physical NICs with driver, speed, and carrier status. Does not require root.

docs.text:
Generate cryptographically random passwords and secrets for deployment.

Option Description --stdout Print secrets to stdout instead of writing to .env --env-file PATH Write to a custom .env path (default: /opt/nettap/.env) --force Regenerate all secrets even if they already exist --dry-run Show what would be done without writing -v, --verbose Debug output -h, --help Show help

docs.title: scripts/common.sh
docs.text:
Shared shell utilities sourced by all other scripts. Provides:

  • Logging: log, warn, error, debug functions
  • Dry-run support: run function wraps commands for --dry-run mode
  • Cleanup traps: push_cleanup, enable_cleanup_trap, disable_cleanup_trap
  • Lock files: acquire_lock, release_lock (prevents concurrent script execution)
  • Retry logic: retry <attempts> <delay> <command> for transient failures

  • Environment loading: load_env reads .env files
  • Network helpers: list_physical_nics, get_nic_driver, nic_has_carrier, get_nic_speed, get_nic_mac

docs.title: Service Management
docs.text:
These are systemd commands, not NetTap scripts, but they are the primary way to manage the running system:

# Start NetTap
sudo systemctl start nettap

# Stop NetTap
sudo systemctl stop nettap

# Restart NetTap
sudo systemctl restart nettap

# Check status
systemctl status nettap

# View logs
journalctl -u nettap -f

# Enable/disable auto-start on boot
sudo systemctl enable nettap
sudo systemctl disable nettap

docker compose -f /opt/nettap/docker/docker-compose.yml ps

docs.title: Configuration Files Reference
docs.text: NetTap uses several configuration files to customize the behavior of Zeek, Suricata, OpenSearch ILM, Grafana, and the hardware watchdog. This page documents each file.

docs.title: config/zeek/nettap.zeek
docs.text:
Zeek script overrides loaded at startup. Mounted into the Zeek container at /opt/zeek/share/zeek/site/local.zeek.

config/zeek/nettap.zeek
# Capture interface — full packet snaplen
redef Pcap::snaplen = 65535;

# Log rotation — batch writes every 30s to reduce SSD wear
redef Log::default_rotation_interval = 30sec;

# Enable JSON output for OpenSearch ingestion
@load policy/tuning/json-logs

# Disable gzip (using zstd in the log pipeline instead)
redef LogAscii::gzip_level = 0;
redef LogAscii::enable_utf_8 = T;

# Load standard protocol analyzers
@load base/protocols/conn
@load base/protocols/dns
@load base/protocols/http
@load base/protocols/ssl
@load base/protocols/dhcp
@load base/protocols/smtp
@load base/files/extract-all-files

# File analysis
@load frameworks/files/hash-all-files

Key settings:

Setting Value Purpose Pcap::snaplen 65535 Capture full packets (not truncated) Log::default_rotation_interval 30sec Batch log writes to reduce SSD wear LogAscii::gzip_level 0 Disable gzip; zstd is used in the log pipeline instead Protocol analyzers conn, dns, http, ssl, dhcp, smtp, files Generate logs for these protocols

Compression strategy: Zeek writes uncompressed JSON logs. The log pipeline (Filebeat -> Logstash) applies zstd compression (~8:1 ratio) before shipping to OpenSearch. This trades temporary disk space for better compression ratios and lower CPU on the capture path.

docs.title: config/suricata/nettap.yaml
docs.text:
A Suricata include file. Mounted at /opt/suricata/include-configs/nettap.yaml; Malcolm's suricata_config_populate.py adds every *.yaml there to the end of the suricata.yaml it generates, so these settings override Malcolm's.

config/suricata/nettap.yaml
%YAML 1.1
---
threshold-file: /etc/nettap/suricata-threshold.config
Setting Value Purpose threshold-file /etc/nettap/suricata-threshold.config Device-local suppress/threshold lines, e.g. one device's alerts for one rule (NET-191). The file lives on the host (/etc/nettap is mounted read-only). If it is missing, Suricata logs a warning and runs with no thresholds.

The file must start with %YAML 1.1 and ---. Without them Suricata refuses the include ("Failed to include configuration file") and suricata-live does not start.

Until 2026-11-07 this file was mounted at /etc/suricata/nettap.yaml, which Malcolm never includes, so its capture and output settings never applied. Capture and eve output come from Malcolm's generated config and the compose environment (SURICATA_*).

docs.title: config/opensearch/ilm-policy.json
docs.text:
The fallback ISM policy file. At startup and on every retention save the daemon builds the policy from your settings instead (daemon/storage/ilm_generator.py) and applies it.

There is one policy:

docs.title: nettap-hot-policy
docs.text:
• Applied to: arkime_sessions3-*, malcolm_beats_* and zeek-* indices. Malcolm writes every Zeek log and Suricata alert into the daily arkime_sessions3-YYMMDD index.
  • Hot state: no rollover (Malcolm starts a new index each day)
  • Delete state: delete each index after RETENTION_HOT days (default 90)
  • Retry: 3 attempts with exponential backoff (10 minute delay)

The older warm (suricata-*) and cold (arkime-*, pcap-*) policies matched no index and were retired. PCAP is files, not an index; the storage daemon prunes them (RETENTION_COLD, PCAP_MAX_DISK_PCT).

docs.title: Grafana Configuration
docs.text:
Grafana is off by default

nettap-grafana only starts with --profile grafana. Its datasources below point at http://opensearch:9200 without a login and at zeek-*/suricata-* indices Malcolm never creates, and its dashboards query raw Zeek and Suricata field names rather than Malcolm's ECS fields, so they show no data. NetTap's own pages cover the same views. See tracking-fixes/2026-11-01-dashboard-data-accuracy.md #71.

docs.title: config/grafana/provisioning/datasources/datasource.yaml
docs.text:
Grafana datasource provisioning. Auto-configures OpenSearch connections on startup.

config/grafana/provisioning/datasources/datasource.yaml
apiVersion: 1
datasources:
  - name: OpenSearch-Zeek
    type: grafana-opensearch-datasource
    access: proxy
    url: http://opensearch:9200
    database: "zeek-*"
    isDefault: true
    jsonData:
      timeField: "ts"
      version: "2.11.0"
      flavor: "opensearch"
    editable: false

  - name: OpenSearch-Suricata
    type: grafana-opensearch-datasource
    access: proxy
    url: http://opensearch:9200
    database: "suricata-*"
    jsonData:
      timeField: "timestamp"
      version: "2.11.0"
      flavor: "opensearch"
    editable: false

Two datasources are configured:

Datasource Index Pattern Time Field Purpose OpenSearch-Zeek zeek-* ts Zeek metadata queries OpenSearch-Suricata suricata-* timestamp Suricata alert queries

docs.title: config/watchdog/watchdog.conf
docs.text:
Hardware watchdog timer configuration. Deployed to /etc/watchdog.conf by scripts/install/setup-watchdog.sh.

config/watchdog/watchdog.conf
watchdog-device = /dev/watchdog
interval = 10
watchdog-timeout = 60
max-load-1 = 24
min-memory = 1
ping = 127.0.0.1
log-dir = /var/log/watchdog
realtime = yes
priority = 1
Setting Value Purpose watchdog-device /dev/watchdog Kernel watchdog device node interval 10s Pet frequency (5 pets per timeout window) watchdog-timeout 60s Hardware reboot trigger if no pet received max-load-1 24 Reboot if 1-minute load average exceeds 24 (6x cores) min-memory 1 page Extreme memory exhaustion failsafe ping 127.0.0.1 Test kernel network stack is alive realtime yes Run with realtime scheduling priority

The watchdog is a last-resort failsafe. If the system hangs, the hardware watchdog triggers a reboot within ~90 seconds, restoring network traffic flow.

docs.title: Suricata rules
docs.text:
Set in docker/docker-compose.yml for suricata-live (NET-191). Malcolm's updater reads them at every update.

Variable Default Description SURICATA_UPDATE_ENABLE_SOURCES et/open,abuse.ch/sslbl-blacklist,echap/stalkerware,ipfire/dbl The rule sources, comma-separated. Each start enables exactly these (stored source configs are wiped first). With an ET Pro code saved, et/open becomes et/pro at start. SURICATA_DISABLE_SIDS 2200121,2231001,re:msg:"IPFire DBL \[(?!Malware\]\|Phishing\]) Lines for /etc/suricata/disable.conf: two decoder rules that fire on switch traffic, and the IPFire DBL allowlist (every category except Malware and Phishing off). SURICATA_UPDATE_RULES true Update rules at start, nightly at 00:00 UTC and on "Update now". SURICATA_UPDATE_ETOPEN removed Unused by Malcolm 26.10.0; upstream would add ET Open beside ET Pro. ET Open is chosen through the source list.

docs.title: ET Pro code
docs.text: Not an environment variable in .env. Settings › Suricata rules writes /etc/nettap/suricata.env (root, mode 600) with one line, SURICATA_ETPRO_CODE=<16-64 letters and digits>. config/capture/nettap-capture-env.sh reads it when suricata-live starts; an invalid value is ignored without being printed. The old SURICATA_ET_PRO_KEY API key field is retired.

docs.title: Rule update wrapper (config/suricata/nettap-rules-update.sh)
docs.text:
State lives on the nettap-rules-state volume (/run/nettap-rules in suricata-live, /var/run/nettap-rules in the daemon): rules.lock, update-status.json, update-in-progress, last-good and its gen-* copies. The overrides below exist for tests.

Variable Default Description NETTAP_RULES_STATE /run/nettap-rules State directory (the daemon reads the same variable) NETTAP_RULES_LOCK_WAIT 900 Seconds an update waits for the rules lock NETTAP_RULES_RELOAD_WAIT 300 Seconds to wait for Suricata to load new or restored rules NETTAP_RULES_RETRY_S 5 Seconds between reload checks NETTAP_RULES_UPDATE_MAX 900 Seconds Malcolm's updater may run before it is stopped (so it can't hold the rules lock) NETTAP_MALCOLM_UPDATE /usr/local/bin/malcolm-suricata-update-rules.sh Malcolm's updater, kept beside the shim NETTAP_RULES_SOURCES_FILE /var/lib/suricata/update/nettap-enable-sources The source list the container started with (for docker exec updates) NETTAP_SURICATA_SOCKET /var/run/suricata/suricata-command.socket Suricata's command socket NETTAP_SURICATA_ENV /etc/nettap/suricata.env Where the loader and the daemon find the ET Pro code

docs.title: Own rules (daemon, NET-191 slice 3)
docs.text:
owner.rules lives on the suricata-custom-rules volume: rw in the daemon, ro in suricata-live at /opt/suricata/rules/custom (Malcolm lists SURICATA_CUSTOM_RULES_DIR/**/*.rules in rule-files at start). Suricata's test of a save runs on snapshots in the nettap-rules-staging volume, which suricata-live never mounts. The limits (2,000 rules, 256 KB) are constants in daemon/services/owner_rules_validator.py. The overrides below exist for tests.

Variable Default Description NETTAP_CUSTOM_RULES_DIR /var/lib/nettap-suricata-custom The daemon's mount of suricata-custom-rules NETTAP_RULES_STAGING_DIR /var/lib/nettap-rules-staging The daemon's mount of nettap-rules-staging; must not be inside the custom rules dir

The test container mounts the staging volume from the host, so the daemon inspects its own container for the volume's host path. That container's name is DAEMON_CONTAINER_NAME, the variable the Malcolm update already uses.

docs.text: NIC Why USB Ethernet adapters Unreliable for sustained packet capture. Buffer overflows under load. Wi-Fi adapters Cannot be used in a Layer 2 bridge. Management-only. Mellanox ConnectX Requires OFED drivers not included in the installer.

docs.title: NIC LED Identification Support
docs.text:
The setup wizard can blink NIC LEDs to help identify physical ports. Support varies by hardware:

NIC Driver LED Blink Support igc (Intel i226-V, i225-V) Yes igb (Intel I350, I210) Yes e1000e (Intel I219) Yes i40e (Intel X710) Yes r8169 (Realtek) Limited (may not work on all models)

LED identification uses ethtool --identify, which requires driver support.

docs.title: Tested SSDs
docs.text:
Model Type Capacity Endurance Notes Samsung 980 Pro NVMe 1 TB 600 TBW Excellent. Fast and durable. WD Black SN770 NVMe 1 TB 600 TBW Good performance/price ratio. Crucial P3 NVMe 1 TB 220 TBW Budget. Adequate for home use. Samsung 870 EVO SATA 1 TB 600 TBW Good SATA option if no M.2 slot.

NVMe SSDs are strongly recommended for their superior random I/O performance (important for OpenSearch queries) and generally higher write endurance.

docs.title: Submit Your Hardware
docs.text:
Tested NetTap on hardware not listed here? Help the community by submitting your results:

  1. Open a GitHub Issue with the "Info" label
  2. Include:
  3. Hardware model and specs (CPU, RAM, storage, NICs)
  4. NIC driver names (ethtool -i eth0)
  5. Ubuntu version
  6. Any issues encountered
  7. Performance observations (throughput, latency, CPU usage)
  8. Or submit a PR editing this page directly

docs.title: NetTap Full Code Review — 2026-10-30
docs.text: Scope: the whole repository at fix/pr110-review (PR #144, b7f48e1), i.e. PR #110 plus its review fixes: daemon (Python), web (SvelteKit), host scripts, Docker/Malcolm stack, config, CI. Method: 14 area reviewers, each paired with an adversarial verifier that tried to refute every claim; a completeness critic plus one gap pass; then (at the owner's request) a dedicated Malcolm-stack reviewer compared against upstream Malcolm v26.02.0 source, with its own verifier. 32 agents in total (owner-approved over the original 30 cap). One extra item (LD-001) was found by the lead while designing DHCP gateway mode. Status: findings only. Nothing here is fixed on this branch; the owner triages. Items the DHCP gateway work had to rewrite are fixed on phase-4/dhcp-gateway-mode and marked below.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
• 273 distinct findings after de-duplication (315 raw reports; 2 refuted and dropped; overlapping reports of the same root cause merged).
  • By severity: 6 CRITICAL, 37 HIGH, 121 MEDIUM, 109 LOW.
  • Verdicts: 255 CONFIRMED (traced in code by the verifier), 18 PLAUSIBLE (real-looking but depends on runtime state the verifier could not prove from the checkout).
  • Sources: 260 from the area review (CR-), 12 from the Malcolm pass (MS-), 1 lead-found (LD-). Eight Malcolm-pass reports duplicated an area finding and were folded into it.
  • 63 findings sit in code the DHCP gateway mode touches; 6 of them are fixed on that branch because it rewrote that code.
  • Nothing was run on the NetTap hardware. Every finding comes from reading code and config.

docs.title: Fix first (recommended order)
docs.text: # IDs Why first 1 MS-001 Root cause of Chain 11: OpenSearch never gets Malcolm's ROLE_* env, so every start regenerates and pushes an EMPTY role mapping. One env block (S effort) should end the bootstrap ritual and the dark-after-reboot failures. 2 CR-003 Any LAN device can reach OpenSearch Dashboards with all_access, including by spoofing X-Forwarded-User/Roles: read or delete all captured data. 3 CR-021, CR-022 Arkime viewer on host :8005 with a public fallback secret; Grafana with admin/nettap and anonymous access: LAN-wide exposure of traffic data. 4 CR-002, CR-001, CR-020, MS-002 Data-loss chain: PCAP never pruned (wrong path, ro mount, two writers), so the emergency prune deletes every OpenSearch index, today's included, every cycle. 5 CR-004 Wizard "Verify Configuration" builds and persists the live bridge, can cut off the management NIC, and reports success only when creation failed. 6 CR-025 nettap.service runs docker compose down on stop, so every reboot recreates OpenSearch (and, with MS-001, breaks auth). 7 CR-034 Login form has no effective rate limit. 8 CR-017, CR-038 Age-based retention never runs: ISM policies match no real index. 9 LD-001 Daemon-written boot units are never enabled (dangling symlink target), so bridge mode may be down after a reboot.

docs.title: Fixed on the DHCP gateway branch
docs.text: ID What changed CR-007 wizard mode/NIC now reach load_capture_config and the capture containers CR-165 configure validates interface names before writing CR-166 configure validates interface names before writing CR-167 storage/SMART loops start first; capture setup guarded with fallback CR-212 dhcp_gateway labelled correctly CR-247 dhcp_gateway labelled correctly

docs.text:
Ranked most severe first. Full text for CRITICAL and HIGH items is in the detail section below. "Tracked" names an existing tracker entry (DEPLOYMENT-ISSUES chain, PR #144 follow-up, security review) when the issue was already known. "DHCP" = in code the DHCP gateway mode touches.

docs.title: CR-001 (CRITICAL) — PCAP cleanup never deletes anything: wrong path, read-only mount, top-level glob only
docs.text:
• Where: daemon/storage/manager.py:108
  • Verdict: CONFIRMED. RetentionConfig.pcap_dir defaults to /data/pcap. Neither _parse_json, _from_env nor main.py ever sets it, and only server.py:914/1134 and pcap_search.py read PCAP_DIR. Dockerfile.daemon never creates /data/pcap, and the container root is read_only, so pcap_dir.exists() is False in all four PCAP paths. compose mounts pcap-data at /opt/nettap/pcap:ro (docker-compose.yml:694), so unlink would hit EROFS even with the right path. The glob is top-level only, and arkime-live writes into the arkime-live/ subdirectory. No other PCAP pruning exists in scripts/config/docker, and arkime-live has MANAGE_PCAP_FILES=false.
  • Tracked: PR #144 follow-up: PCAP cleanup path
  • Issue: RetentionConfig.pcap_dir defaults to /data/pcap, and nothing sets it from the PCAP_DIR env var that compose passes (/opt/nettap/pcap). Only server.py reads PCAP_DIR, for TShark and PCAP search. /data/pcap does not exist in the daemon container, so _delete_oldest_pcaps(), get_tier_usage(), preview_cleanup() and execute_cleanup() find no PCAP. Even with the right path, compose mounts pcap-data into the daemon read-only (docker-compose.yml:694 pcap-data:/opt/nettap/pcap:ro), so unlink() would fail with EROFS. The glob is also top-level only (*.pcap), while arkime-live writes into the arkime-live/ subdirectory. arkime-live runs with MANAGE_PCAP_FILES=false, so nothing else limits PCAP growth.
  • Failure scenario: pcap-capture (100 MB / 10 min rotation) and arkime-live write PCAP without limit. The emergency cascade logs 'PCAP directory /data/pcap does not exist' at debug level and frees nothing.
