The disk reaches 100%, OpenSearch, Redis AOF and Logstash fail, and the manual 'cleanup' preview shows 0 PCAP files and 0 PCAP bytes.
  • Fix: Build RetentionConfig.pcap_dir from PCAP_DIR. Mount pcap-data read-write in the daemon, or set MANAGE_PCAP_FILES=true with an Arkime freeSpaceG limit. Use rglob('*.pcap'). Catch FileNotFoundError from the stat() sort key, which can race with rotation. (effort S)

docs.title: CR-002 (CRITICAL) — Emergency prune deletes every OpenSearch index, today's live index included, and repeats every cycle
docs.text:
• Where: daemon/storage/manager.py:462
  • Verdict: CONFIRMED. prune_emergency() (manager.py:436-480) sorts every dated index oldest-first, has no check that skips today's index (preview_cleanup and execute_cleanup do skip it, prune_emergency does not), and only stops once usage < disk_threshold. When PCAP fills the disk, deleting indices never brings usage under 80%. PCAP fill is reachable: capture is on by default (PCAP_CAPTURE_ENABLED defaults to true), arkime-live runs with MANAGE_PCAP_FILES=false, and _delete_oldest_pcaps never finds a file (claim 1). The daemon checks '/', which in the container is the docker overlay on the same filesystem as the pcap-data volume. run_cycle sends usage >= 0.90 to emergency_cascade every 300 s, so today's arkime_sessions3-YYMMDD index is deleted again on every cycle.
  • Tracked: new (the trigger, PCAP never being cleaned, is tracked as PR #144 follow-up: PC…
  • Issue: prune_emergency() sorts every dated index oldest-first across all tiers, with no protection for today's index and no minimum to keep. It keeps deleting until usage drops below disk_threshold (80%), not the emergency threshold. emergency_cascade() calls it before delete_oldest_pcaps(). When something other than OpenSearch is filling the disk (PCAP, Docker images, logs), deleting indices never gets usage under 80%. The loop then deletes every index: all arkime_sessions3-* (Zeek and Suricata), malcolm_beats, nettap-smart- and nettap-changelog-*, including the one being written today. storage_loop runs this again every 300 s while usage stays at or above 90%. Each run deletes the arkime_sessions3- index that Logstash has just recreated.
  • Failure scenario: In the default compose, PCAP is never deleted (see the PCAP finding). Full-packet capture from netsniff-ng and arkime-live fills the 1 TB NVMe to 90%. The cycle deletes all metadata and alerts, still sits above 80% because PCAP makes up most of the disk, and from then on deletes today's index every 5 minutes. The dashboard stays empty and all detection history is lost, while the disk keeps filling toward 100%.
  • Fix: Never delete indices dated today (better, keep the newest N days). Delete PCAP before indices in the cascade. Stop index deletion once usage is below emergency_threshold, or once only protected indices remain, and log or alert at CRITICAL that index deletion cannot recover the space rather than wiping everything. (effort S)

docs.title: CR-003 (CRITICAL) — OpenSearch Dashboards is published on :443 with no authentication and all_access backend credentials
docs.text:
• Where: docker/nginx.conf:187
  • Verdict: CONFIRMED. The defect is real, but the claim gets the mechanism wrong. Its assumption is false: the Malcolm v26.02.0 dashboards image is built FROM opensearchproject/opensearch-dashboards:3.5.0 and does NOT remove securityDashboards. Its opensearch_dashboards.yml sets opensearch_security.auth.type [basicauth, proxy] with proxycache user_header X-Forwarded-User and roles_header X-Forwarded-Roles. A plain request without headers therefore gets the OSD login page. The bypass is header spoofing. NetTap's nginx location /dashboards/ (nginx.conf:187) does not strip or overwrite X-Forwarded-User or X-Forwarded-Roles, and it sets X-Forwarded-For. The OSD ProxyAuthentication.requestIncludesAuthInfo check passes when XFF and the user header are both present. OSD forwards those headers (they are on its requestHeadersAllowlist). Malcolm's OpenSearch config.yml, which NetTap does not override, has proxy_auth_domain at order 0 with a noop backend and xff.internalProxies '.*', so it trusts the headers from any peer. NetTap's roles_mapping maps backend role 'admin' to all_access (deploy-malcolm.sh:432). Result: any LAN client that sends X-Forwarded-User: x and X-Forwarded-Roles: admin to https:///dashboards/ is all_access. It can read or delete every index through /dashboards/api/console/proxy. Any container on the Docker network, or any host-networked process via 127.0.0.1:9200, can send the same headers to OpenSearch directly. Severity stays CRITICAL.
  • Tracked: new
  • Issue: nginx proxies location /dashboards/ straight to nettap-dashboards:5601. There is no auth_request and the SvelteKit session gate never sees the request. NetTap disabled Malcolm's nginx-proxy (docker-compose.yml ~613-626), which is where Malcolm puts user authentication. The dashboards container gets the curlrc mount (docker-compose.yml ~190), so it talks to OpenSearch as malcolm_internal. deploy-malcolm.sh:414-456 maps that user's admin backend role to all_access. Every Dashboards request therefore runs as an OpenSearch superuser. The Infrastructure page even links users to /dashboards/ (web/src/routes/infrastructure/+page.svelte:1211). One assumption: this relies on Malcolm's dashboards image shipping without the securityDashboards plugin. Malcolm removes that plugin because its nginx-proxy does the auth. I could not check the image from this checkout.
  • *Malcolm pass adds: nettap-nginx serves /dashboards/ to the whole LAN on 0.0.0.0:443 with no auth, and it passes client-supplied headers through unchanged. Malcolm's Dashboards config sets opensearch_security.auth.type [basicauth, proxy] and allowlists X-Forwarded-User and X-Forwarded-Roles. Malcolm's OpenSearch security config.yml has proxy_auth_domain at order 0 with xff.internalProxies '.'. NetTap maps backend role 'admin' to all_access. Upstream Malcolm is only safe because its nginx-proxy authenticates the user and overwrites these headers. NetTap replaced that proxy and does neither. OpenSearch on 127.0.0.1:9200 accepts the same headers from any host-networked or docker-network container without a password.
  • Failure scenario: Any device on the management LAN opens https:///dashboards/app/dev_tools#/console with no login. It sends GET _cat/indices and GET arkime_sessions3-*/_search to read every captured connection, DNS query and alert. Or it sends DELETE arkime_sessions3-*,zeek-*,suricata-* (through /dashboards/api/console/proxy with an osd-xsrf: true header) and wipes all stored network history. A compromised container on the default Docker network, such as nettap-tshark parsing attacker PCAPs, can reach dashboards:5601 directly and do the same.
  • Fix: Remove the /dashboards/ location from nginx.conf, or gate it with auth_request on a SvelteKit endpoint that checks the nettap_token cookie (return 401 otherwise). Also remove the dashboards link until that gate exists. (effort S)

docs.title: CR-004 (CRITICAL) — Wizard 'Verify Configuration' creates the live bridge, and reports success only when creation failed
docs.text:
• Where: web/src/routes/setup/+page.svelte:368, daemon/api/bridge.py:168, web/src/routes/api/setup/bridge/+server.ts:40, web/src/routes/api/setup/bridge/+server.ts:45, web/src/routes/api/setup/bridge/+server.ts:49
  • Verdict: CONFIRMED. verifyBridge POSTs /api/setup/bridge. The web proxy calls the daemon's /api/setup/bridge, which bridge.py:248 routes to handle_bridge_create. That calls BridgeManager.create_bridge with persist=True by default: nsenter enslaves both NICs, turns on promisc, runs the sysctl changes and writes the netplan, systemd and sysctl files. On success the daemon returns {created, state, ...} with no ready field, so bridgeVerified stays false and nothing renders. On failure the daemon returns 400 with an errors list. daemonJSON turns that into an error, and the proxy falls back to a mock with ready:true, so the wizard shows 'Configuration verified successfully' and writes localStorage. The copy at 1227-1228 says no changes will be made. The selectors only disable the other selected NIC; nothing blocks the NIC that carries the management IP. The daemon has pid:host and the capabilities nsenter needs, so the changes really happen.
  • Tracked: new
  • Issue: verifyBridge() POSTs to /api/setup/bridge. The web route proxies that to the daemon's POST /api/setup/bridge, which is handle_bridge_create (daemon/api/bridge.py:248). That handler runs BridgeManager.create_bridge(persist=True): it enslaves both NICs to br0 over nsenter and writes netplan, systemd and sysctl persistence files. The step's own copy says 'No changes will be made to your network until then' (line 1227). The result handling is also backwards. A successful daemon create returns {created, state, errors...} with no ready field, so bridgeVerified stays false and the wizard shows nothing. A failed create (400 or 503) makes daemonJSON return an error, so web/src/routes/api/setup/bridge/+server.ts:52-75 falls back to a MOCK preview with ready:true, and the wizard shows 'Configuration verified successfully'. The WAN/LAN selectors (lines 1092-1126) do not block the NIC that carries the management IP the browser is using.
  • Failure scenario: The target box is an N100 with two i226-V NICs. The user reaches the wizard over enp1s0, which has a DHCP address from the router. They pick WAN=enp1s0 and LAN=enp2s0, then click 'Verify Configuration'. The daemon enslaves enp1s0 into br0 and persists it, so the browser loses the appliance mid-wizard. No admin account exists yet, and the box comes back unreachable after a reboot too. On a box where the daemon rejects the NICs, the wizard instead shows a green 'verified' mock config.
  • Fix: Point the wizard at a non-mutating endpoint: a preview, or GET /api/bridge/readiness plus NIC validation. Leave bridge creation to Go Live. Delete the mock fallback in api/setup/bridge/+server.ts and show the daemon error. Block or loudly warn on a WAN/LAN NIC that has an IPv4 address or the default route. (effort M)

docs.title: MS-001 (CRITICAL) — OpenSearch lacks ROLE_ADMIN, so every container start wipes the role mapping and pushes the empty one
docs.text:
• Where: docker/docker-compose.yml:98
  • Verdict: CONFIRMED. The opensearch.Dockerfile uses sed to put setup-internal-users.sh in place of the 'Disabling execution of install_demo_configuration' line, so it runs on every entrypoint start, plain restarts included (NetTap sets DISABLE_INSTALL_DEMO_CONFIG=true). That script runs envsubst on roles_mapping.yml.orig, where every entry is $ROLE_*, then yq 'del(.[] \| select(.backend_roles and (.backend_roles[] == "")))'. No ROLE_* variable is set: NetTap has no env_file, the opensearch service has no ROLE_ADMIN, and docker/.env holds no ROLE_* (and is used only for interpolation anyway). So only _meta survives, which is exactly the Chain 11 symptom ('only _meta header'). setup-post-start.sh then runs securityadmin.sh -cd ... -h opensearch in the background and pushes it. container_health.sh's curl --fail https://localhost:9200 gets 403, opensearch goes unhealthy, and the service_healthy dependents never start. Nothing in the repo re-runs securityadmin automatically: it is only in deploy-malcolm.sh and the remote fix scripts.
  • Tracked: DEPLOYMENT-ISSUES Chain 11, Chain 15 Fix 5 and Known Risks (symptom only; root…
  • Related: CR-025
  • Issue: Malcolm's opensearch image runs setup-internal-users.sh on every start (it replaces the 'Disabling execution of install_demo_configuration' line in opensearch-docker-entrypoint.sh). That script rebuilds roles_mapping.yml from roles_mapping.yml.orig with envsubst ($ROLE_ADMIN, $ROLE_CAPTURE_SERVICE, $ROLE_READ_ACCESS, ...), then runs yq 'del(.[] \| select(.backend_roles[] == ""))'. NetTap's opensearch service never sets the auth-common.env variables (ROLE_ADMIN=admin and the others), so every entry is deleted and only _meta is left. setup-post-start.sh then runs securityadmin.sh (-h opensearch) in the background and pushes that EMPTY mapping into .opendistro_security. This is the real root cause of Chain 11. The file does not 'revert to the image default': it is regenerated empty and re-pushed on EVERY start, plain restarts included. The bootstrap in deploy-malcolm.sh (and fix-opensearch.sh) also races the post-start push: whichever securityadmin run finishes last wins.
  • Failure scenario: After a host reboot, nettap.service runs ExecStop=docker compose down, then up -d on boot (scripts/install/install.sh:394). The same happens after an OOM restart or a docker restart nettap-opensearch. malcolm_internal authenticates but has no roles, so every request gets 403. container_health.sh fails and opensearch goes unhealthy. depends_on service_healthy then blocks dashboards, logstash, the daemon, nettap-web and grafana, and through the daemon also zeek-live, suricata-live, pcap-capture and arkime-live. The appliance is dark until someone runs fix-opensearch.sh by hand. On a fresh deploy, auth randomly works or fails depending on the securityadmin race.
  • Fix: Add the auth-common.env role variables to the opensearch environment (at least ROLE_ADMIN: "admin" and ROLE_CAPTURE_SERVICE: "capture_service", ideally all ROLE_* from config/auth-common.env.example). Malcolm's own entrypoint then produces the correct mapping on every start. Remove the manual roles_mapping overwrite from deploy-malcolm.sh and fix-opensearch.sh, and drop the CLAUDE.md bootstrap ritual. Verify with: docker restart nettap-opensearch, then a curl with the curlrc to /_cluster/health still returns 200. (effort S)

docs.title: MS-002 (CRITICAL) — Full-time PCAP capture has no retention; emergency prune then deletes all OpenSearch data
docs.text:
• Where: docker/docker-compose.yml:694
  • Verdict: CONFIRMED. pcap-capture runs netsniff-ng (PCAP_ENABLE_NETSNIFF=true), and capture_control treats PCAP_CAPTURE_ENABLED as true by default. netsniff-ng writes to /pcap at the root of pcap-data, and MANAGE_PCAP_FILES=false. RetentionConfig.pcap_dir defaults to '/data/pcap', and neither RetentionConfigManager._from_env nor _parse_json sets it. PCAP_DIR is read only by the tshark and pcap_search services. In the daemon the volume is at /opt/nettap/pcap:ro, so _delete_oldest_pcaps and the manual cleanup find no directory and do nothing. The capture stop flag is the daemon's own /tmp/nettap-stop-capture, which no capture container reads. prune_emergency deletes every dated index, oldest first, regardless of tier. OpenSearch has disk.threshold_enabled=false. Nothing else in the repo prunes pcap-data.
  • Tracked: new
  • Related: CR-001, CR-002, CR-020
  • Issue: pcap-capture runs netsniff-ng full-packet capture on br0 continuously (PCAP_ENABLE_NETSNIFF=true, PCAP_CAPTURE_ENABLED defaults to true). arkime-live is configured for a second full capture into the same volume. Nothing prunes pcap-data. The daemon's RetentionConfig.pcap_dir defaults to /data/pcap (daemon/storage/manager.py:108), and retention_config.py never applies the PCAP_DIR env. That path does not exist in the daemon container, where the volume is mounted at /opt/nettap/pcap, and the mount is :ro anyway. _delete_oldest_pcaps and execute_cleanup are therefore no-ops. The 95% 'stop capture' flag is written to the daemon's own /tmp, which no capture container reads. OpenSearch has cluster.routing.allocation.disk.threshold_enabled=false, so it has no read-only safety net either.
  • Failure scenario: At an average of 20 Mbps the PCAP volume grows about 200 GB/day, so a 1 TB NVMe passes 90% within days. run_cycle → emergency_cascade → prune_emergency deletes every dated OpenSearch index oldest-first, including all arkime_sessions3-* Zeek and Suricata history. PCAP deletion silently does nothing, and capture is never stopped. The disk still reaches 100%. OpenSearch writes fail with ENOSPC, and Zeek, Suricata and Logstash stall. Result: all telemetry is lost and the stack is down.
  • Fix: Mount pcap-data read-write in the daemon and pass pcap_dir from PCAP_DIR (/opt/nettap/pcap) into RetentionConfig. Glob recursively, because netsniff writes to the root and arkime to arkime-live/. Make the critical threshold actually stop capture (docker stop nettap-pcap-capture via the existing capture_control helper). Pick ONE full-capture engine: disable netsniff when arkime-live is used, or set ARKIME_LIVE_CAPTURE=false. Consider Arkime's freeSpaceG/MANAGE_PCAP_FILES=true so Arkime prunes its own PCAP. Make PCAP time-based retention (cold_days) run regardless of disk %. (effort M)

docs.title: CR-005 (HIGH) — Suricata decoder-noise filter never matches anything
docs.text:
• Where: daemon/api/alerts.py:51
  • Verdict: CONFIRMED. _SURICATA_NOISE_EXCLUSION is {prefix: {rule.name: 'SURICATA '}}. The repo's own records say Malcolm indexes strings as text plus a keyword multi-field (DEPLOYMENT-ISSUES issue 13, commit 43b0394, comment at alerts.py:348), and every aggregation uses rule.name.keyword. Prefix is a term-level query and is not analyzed. An uppercase value that ends in a space can never match the lowercase single tokens of a standard-analyzed text field, so the must_not does nothing. traffic.py:682 has the same clause. Only get_smart_alerts filters noise, through ENGINE_NOISE_SIGNATURES.
  • Tracked: new
  • Issue: _SURICATA_NOISE_EXCLUSION is {"prefix": {"rule.name": "SURICATA "}}. rule.name is an analyzed text field holding lowercase single tokens (commit 43b0394 and the comment at alerts.py:348). A prefix query is not analyzed, so an uppercase prefix that ends in a space can never match a token. The must_not in the list, count, categories, category detail and category timeline handlers is therefore a no-op. The timeline, top-signatures and top-ips handlers don't apply the filter at all. The same broken clause is in daemon/api/traffic.py:682 and daemon/services/live_connections.py:315.
  • Failure scenario: A capture with truncated packets produces millions of 'SURICATA AF-PACKET truncated packet' alerts. /api/alerts/count, the alert list and the category cards all count them as real alerts, and the decoder noise buries the ET signatures, which is exactly what the filter was meant to stop.
  • Fix: Use {"prefix": {"rule.name.keyword": "SURICATA "}}, matching the other keyword-based queries. Apply the same exclusion in timeline, top-signatures and top-ips so chart totals match the counts. Fix the copies in traffic.py and live_connections.py too. Add a test that checks the field name. (effort S)

docs.title: CR-006 (HIGH) — Synchronous OpenSearch calls block the daemon's event loop
docs.text:
• Where: daemon/api/alerts.py:404
  • Verdict: CONFIRMED. alerts.py has 9 client.search calls and devices.py has 10, all run directly inside async handlers. The client is the sync opensearchpy OpenSearch from StorageManager with timeout=30, max_retries=3 and retry_on_timeout=True, so one call can block for about 2 minutes. server.py already uses run_in_executor for the storage, SMART and logs calls, but the alert and device handlers don't. The compose healthcheck calls /api/health with a 15s timeout. Reaching the worst case needs OpenSearch to be slow, but the loop-blocking pattern itself is certain.
  • Tracked: new (same class as the IoT/storage executor fixes in PR #110: 68b129b, fd05119)
  • Issue: Every alerts.py handler (9 calls) and devices.py handler (10 calls plus the fingerprint lookups) calls the synchronous opensearch-py client directly inside async def. The client is built with timeout=30, max_retries=3 and retry_on_timeout=True (storage/manager.py:188). One slow or hung query can freeze the single event loop for up to about 2 minutes. During that time every other daemon request waits: /api/health, setup, bridge bypass, capture status, and the web's parallel page loads. PR #110 already moved IoT (68b129b) and the storage cycle (fd05119) onto executors for this reason, but the alert and device handlers were not changed.
  • Failure scenario: OpenSearch is under merge or ILM pressure on the N100. The alerts page fires 6 aggregations at once with Promise.allSettled. They run one after another on the loop, each up to 30s. Meanwhile the compose healthcheck on /api/health and a user's 'Enable bypass' click hang until they time out.
  • Fix: Wrap client.search in await loop.run_in_executor(None, ...) (or asyncio.to_thread) through one shared helper in alerts.py and devices.py, as IoT does. Over time, move to opensearch-py's AsyncOpenSearch. (effort M)

docs.title: CR-007 (HIGH) — Setup wizard's capture mode and NIC choice never reach the daemon or the capture containers
docs.text:
• Where: daemon/api/setup.py:24, daemon/api/setup.py:65, daemon/services/capture_config.py:32, web/src/routes/api/setup/configure/+server.ts:15
  • Verdict: CONFIRMED. The wizard (web/src/routes/setup/+page.svelte:599-628) posts to the daemon's handle_setup_configure. That handler writes bare KEY=VALUE lines to /opt/nettap/data/capture-mode.conf and CAPTURE_MODE/CAPTURE_INTERFACE/WAN_IFACE to /opt/nettap/data/.env. load_capture_config (main.py:474 and capture_mode_stub.py:39) reads only CAPTURE_CONFIG_PATH or /etc/nettap/capture-mode.conf as INI, and otherwise os.environ CAPTURE_MODE, PCAP_IFACE and MANAGEMENT_IFACE. Compose sets those from ${CAPTURE_MODE:-bridge} and ${PCAP_IFACE:-br0}, does not set CAPTURE_CONFIG_PATH, and has no env_file. The only code that reads data/.env is retention (RETENTION_*) and enforce_capture_state (PCAP_CAPTURE_ENABLED). save_capture_config and write_env_file have no callers outside tests, and the install scripts never set CAPTURE_MODE. A mirror choice in the wizard is therefore never applied.
  • Tracked: new (distinct from the PR #144 follow-up 'capture settings have no effect', whi…
  • Issue: POST /api/setup/configure writes /opt/nettap/data/capture-mode.conf as bare KEY=VALUE lines. It also writes CAPTURE_MODE, CAPTURE_INTERFACE, MANAGEMENT_INTERFACE, WAN_IFACE and LAN_IFACE into /opt/nettap/data/.env, which sits inside the nettap-appdata volume. Nothing reads either file. load_capture_config() (services/capture_config.py:62) reads CAPTURE_CONFIG_PATH or /etc/nettap/capture-mode.conf, and expects INI [capture]/[bridge] sections, which this format would fail to parse (MissingSectionHeaderError). When that file is missing it falls back to os.environ CAPTURE_MODE, PCAP_IFACE and MANAGEMENT_IFACE. Compose takes those from docker/.env (${CAPTURE_MODE:-bridge}, ${PCAP_IFACE:-br0}) and has no env_file. The key names also differ (CAPTURE_INTERFACE vs PCAP_IFACE, MANAGEMENT_INTERFACE vs MANAGEMENT_IFACE). The proper writers, save_capture_config() and write_env_file(), are never called, and the daemon root FS is read_only, so /etc/nettap is not writable anyway.
  • Failure scenario: A user picks Mirror/SPAN on enp2s0 in the wizard and gets 200 {status: ok, files_written: [...]}. After a restart the daemon still loads mode=bridge (BridgeCaptureAdapter), and /api/capture/mode reports bridge. zeek-live, suricata-live and pcap-capture keep listening on br0, which does not exist in a mirror deployment. Result: zero capture, and no error is shown anywhere.
  • Fix: Write through services.capture_config.save_capture_config() and write_env_file() to a path in a writable volume, and set CAPTURE_CONFIG_PATH and CAPTURE_ENV_PATH in compose. Feed PCAP_IFACE to the capture services through a host-side env file or script, since compose interpolation reads docker/.env on the host. Validate interface names against discover_interfaces(), reject wan_interface == lan_interface, and return an explicit 'restart required' state. A new DHCP-gateway mode needs this same path, so fix it before adding a third mode. (effort M)
  • Status: fixed on phase-4/dhcp-gateway-mode — wizard mode/NIC now reach load_capture_config and the capture containers.

docs.title: CR-008 (HIGH) — Alert suppressions, false-positive marks, baselines and the TI cache are written to tmpfs /tmp and lost on every restart
docs.text:
• Where: daemon/services/alert_intelligence.py:889, daemon/services/alert_intelligence.py:890
  • Verdict: CONFIRMED. _SUPPRESS_PATH, _BASELINE_PATH and _TI_CACHE_PATH all default to NETTAP_DATA_DIR or '/tmp'. NETTAP_DATA_DIR is not set anywhere in docker-compose.yml or Dockerfile.daemon (a repo-wide grep finds it only in setup.py and web code). The daemon is read_only with /tmp as a 50M tmpfs, which is emptied on every container restart or recreate. The persistent nettap-appdata volume at /opt/nettap/data is not used for these files.
  • Tracked: new
  • Issue: _SUPPRESS_PATH, _BASELINE_PATH and threat_intel._TI_CACHE_PATH default to NETTAP_DATA_DIR or '/tmp'. NETTAP_DATA_DIR is not set for nettap-storage-daemon in docker-compose.yml or Dockerfile.daemon. The container is read_only, and /tmp is a 50M tmpfs.
  • Failure scenario: A user marks 'ET POLICY ...' as a false positive and suppresses a noisy signature for 30 days. Any daemon restart, redeploy or reboot of the appliance (the deploy scripts use --force-recreate) wipes /tmp. Every suppressed alert comes back in smart alerts and the threat score, and the baseline history starts over.
  • Fix: Default these paths to /opt/nettap/data (the nettap-appdata volume), as api/setup.py already does, or set NETTAP_DATA_DIR=/opt/nettap/data in the daemon's compose environment. Write atomically (tmp file + os.replace). (effort S)

docs.title: CR-009 (HIGH) — Smart Alerts silently drop alert groups past the first 200 composite buckets
docs.text:
• Where: daemon/services/alert_intelligence.py:1181
  • Verdict: CONFIRMED. get_smart_alerts runs a composite aggregation of size 200 over (rule.name.keyword, source.ip.keyword, destination.ip.keyword) and never reads after_key. No after_key handling exists anywhere in the daemon. Composite buckets come back in ascending key order, so 'ET DNS', 'ET INFO' and 'ET POLICY' triples fill the page ahead of 'ET SCAN' and 'ET TROJAN'. get_smart_alert_summary builds on get_smart_alerts, so the summary has the same gap.
  • Tracked: new
  • Issue: get_smart_alerts (used by GET /api/alerts/smart and /smart/summary) runs a composite aggregation over (rule.name.keyword, source.ip.keyword, destination.ip.keyword) with size 200. It never follows after_key. Composite buckets come back in ascending key order, not by severity or count, so only the 200 alphabetically first (signature, src, dst) triples are ever looked at.
  • Failure scenario: In a 7-day window, 'ET DNS…', 'ET INFO…' and 'ET POLICY…' alerts across many destinations make up more than 200 triples. An 'ET TROJAN …' or 'ET SCAN …' alert sorts after them, so it never appears on Smart Alerts or in the kill-chain summary, even though /api/alerts/count includes it.
  • Fix: Page through the composite with after_key up to a sane cap, or replace it with a terms aggregation on rule.name.keyword ordered by severity/count with src/dst sub-aggregations. Return a 'truncated' flag when the cap is hit. (effort M)

docs.title: CR-010 (HIGH) — Bypass enable reports success but does not stop inspection
docs.text:
• Where: daemon/services/bridge_health.py:317, daemon/services/bridge_health.py:331
  • Verdict: CONFIRMED. trigger_bypass sets _bypass_active, logs a warning when ip link set <iface> promisc off fails, and always returns bypass_active:true with the 'traffic is flowing uninspected' message. The API's BridgeHealthMonitor (server.py:1017-1019) is a separate instance from the one in main.py. WAN_IFACE and LAN_IFACE are not set in compose, so it starts with eth0/eth1. _discover_interfaces only runs inside check_health. Even with the right names, promisc off only clears the user (gflags) promisc reference. The bridge keeps its own promiscuity count on the ports, and Zeek, Suricata and Arkime capture on br0 (PCAP_IFACE=br0), so capture continues. The defect sits in bridge_health.trigger_bypass. The handler only passes its result through.
  • Tracked: new (BRIDGE-ARCHITECTURE.md §7 and RELIABILITY-TRACKER list 'Bypass didn't togg…
  • Issue: handle_bypass_enable returns 200 'Bypass mode activated -- traffic is flowing uninspected' whatever trigger_bypass did. trigger_bypass (services/bridge_health.py:317) only logs a warning when either ip link set <member> promisc off fails. Even when the command works it does not stop capture. promisc off only clears the user promisc flag, and the bridge keeps its own promiscuity count on the member ports. Zeek, Suricata, Arkime and pcap all capture on br0 (PCAP_IFACE=br0) with their own PACKET_MR_PROMISC membership, so forwarded frames still reach them. The API's BridgeHealthMonitor instance (server.py:1019) is also separate from the bridge_loop instance in main.py. It starts with the WAN_IFACE/LAN_IFACE fallbacks eth0/eth1, which are unset in compose, and only discovers the real members inside check_health(). So a bypass sent right after a daemon restart targets NICs that don't exist, and the API still reports success.
  • Failure scenario: On an N100 (enp2s0/enp3s0), the user restarts the daemon and clicks Bypass at once. nsenter runs ip link set eth0 promisc off, which fails. The API still returns bypass_active:true and the UI shows bypass, while every packet keeps being captured, indexed and alerted on. Even with the right NIC names, capture on br0 continues.
  • Fix: Make bypass stop the capture containers (docker stop zeek-live suricata-live arkime-live pcap-capture, as in the manual procedure in BRIDGE-ARCHITECTURE.md), or detach the capture sockets from br0. Return 500 with the errors when any step fails. Call _discover_interfaces() at the start of trigger_bypass/disable_bypass, or share one BridgeHealthMonitor between main.py and the API. (effort M)

docs.title: CR-011 (HIGH) — create_bridge has no management-NIC guard, no name validation and no rollback on partial failure
docs.text:
• Where: daemon/services/bridge_manager.py:154
  • Verdict: CONFIRMED. create_bridge only checks ip -j link show <name> rc. Nothing in bridge_manager.py or api/bridge.py checks for the management NIC or the default route; setup-bridge.sh has a --mgmt guard, but the daemon path does not. Ports are enslaved one at a time (lines 154-171). If the second master call fails, the function returns state 'error' and br0 stays with the first NIC enslaved and set promisc on, with no rollback. One small inaccuracy: offload and IPv6 changes run after that early return, so they are not applied in the failure case. The core defect (management NIC lost, no rollback) stands, and the wizard Verify button can reach it (claim 0).
  • Tracked: new
  • Issue: create_bridge only checks that each name passes ip -j link show <name> (rc 0). It never refuses a NIC that holds the host's management IP or default route, and never validates the name format. The string 'up' passes, because ip link show up lists running links. Ports are enslaved one at a time (lines 154-171). If the second one fails, it returns state 'error' and leaves br0 in place with the first NIC enslaved, promiscuous, offloads off and IPv6 disabled. It does not undo anything.
  • Failure scenario: wan=enp2s0 (management NIC), lan=wlp1s0 (Wi-Fi, which the bridge rejects with 'Device does not allow enslaving'). enp2s0 is enslaved, then the LAN step fails and the call returns an error. The appliance has now lost IP connectivity on its management NIC, and the caller is told only that creation failed. The same happens with any name that passes ip link show but fails ip link set ... master.
  • Fix: Validate names against ^[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]{1,15}$ and against NIC discovery. Refuse any interface that carries the default route or the address the request came in on (MGMT_INTERFACE/MGMT_IP are already in the daemon env). On any enslave error, roll back: nomaster the ports already added, and delete br0 if this call created it. (effort M)

docs.title: CR-012 (HIGH) — Backup and restore read and write config files that the services never use
docs.text:
• Where: daemon/services/config_backup.py:39, daemon/services/config_backup.py:42, web/src/routes/settings/backup/+page.svelte:176, web/src/routes/settings/backup/+page.svelte:313
  • Verdict: CONFIRMED. ConfigBackup defaults to capture_config.json, which nothing reads or writes, and retention_config.json, while RetentionConfigManager and main.py use retention.json. device_aliases reads baseline['aliases'], but DeviceBaseline stores a flat MAC dict and loads any dict wholesale as _known_devices, so an imported 'aliases' key becomes a bogus device entry. Import still lists those sections in applied. Notification and excluded-IP writes land on the correct paths (notifications.json, excluded_ips.json), but nothing reloads the in-memory services.
  • Tracked: new
  • Issue: ConfigBackup paths do not match the files the services use. capture_config is /opt/nettap/data/capture_config.json, which nothing writes or reads; the real capture config is capture-mode.conf plus env. retention_config is retention_config.json, but RetentionConfigManager uses retention.json. device_aliases reads baseline['aliases'], but device_baseline.json is a flat MAC to device dict with no aliases key. On import, writes go to the unused files and the sections are still listed in applied. The aliases import adds an 'aliases' key to device_baseline.json, which DeviceBaseline then loads as a known device MAC. Notification and excluded-IP imports land on disk, but the running NotificationHub and app['excluded_ips'] keep their in-memory state, and the next save overwrites the restored file.
  • Failure scenario: After replacing the SSD, the user restores a backup. The export already had storage_retention={}, capture_mode_config={} and device_aliases={}. The import returns success with applied=[capture_mode_config, storage_retention, ...]. Retention stays at the defaults, the capture settings are gone, the device baseline gains a bogus 'aliases' device, and adding a notification channel later wipes the restored channels.
  • Fix: Point each section at the real store: retention.json through RetentionConfigManager, the capture config through save_capture_config, and baseline entries for aliases. Apply imports through the live service objects (NotificationHub, app['excluded_ips'], the retention manager) instead of raw file writes. Report only the sections that were really applied. (effort M)

docs.title: CR-013 (HIGH) — get_mac_for_ip reads a flat 'source.mac' key that OpenSearch never returns, so every device has no MAC
docs.text:
• Where: daemon/services/device_fingerprint.py:186
  • Verdict: CONFIRMED. Both lookups request _source:["source.mac"] and then read the flat key _source.get("source.mac") (lines 186 and 220). OpenSearch source filtering returns the document's nested shape, and the index is arkime_sessions3-* (docker-compose.yml:733), where Arkime and Malcolm store source as a nested object with mac as an array. DeviceRegistry reads both shapes (device_registry.py:437). The only tests (test_device_fingerprint.py:212,226) mock a flat dict. devices.py:345 and :629 call this for every IP, so mac and manufacturer are always null and the UniFi MAC alias path is never taken.
  • Tracked: new
  • Issue: Both strategies request _source: ["source.mac"] and then read hits[0]["_source"].get("source.mac") (lines 186 and 220). OpenSearch returns source filtering as the document's own nested shape, {"source": {"mac": ...}}. Commit b0992a4 says the Arkime documents are nested, and DeviceRegistry handles both shapes. The tests mock a flat dict, which hides this. In production the lookup always returns None. In Arkime source.mac is usually an array as well, so a plain nested lookup would also need flattening.
  • Failure scenario: GET /api/devices (and the device detail page) calls get_mac_for_ip for every IP. Both queries find a session but return None, so every device shows mac=null and manufacturer=null. UniFi alias lookup by MAC is skipped, and every device falls back to the stale IP-based alias path (see the UniFi finding). That costs 2 wasted OpenSearch round trips per device per page load.
  • Fix: Read src.get("source", {}).get("mac") with the flat key as a fallback, as device_registry does. Flatten a list to its first element. Normalize to upper-case colon form. Change the test mocks to the nested Arkime shape. (effort S)

docs.title: CR-014 (HIGH) — The nettap-devices registry is never populated: no production code calls register_device or any enrich_* method
docs.text:
• Where: daemon/services/device_registry.py:395
  • Verdict: CONFIRMED. Outside daemon/tests, register_device and the enrich_* methods are called only inside device_registry.py itself. server.py:1077 builds the registry, and devices_v2.py registers only GET routes for it. Nothing else writes to nettap-devices. In mirror mode +page.svelte:127-133 fetches getRegistryDevices() and renders DeviceGrid/NewDeviceBanner (lines 503, 551) from it, so both stay empty. acknowledgeDevice sends PATCH (devices-registry.ts:102-110). No daemon route handles PATCH, and the catch-all proxy exports only GET, POST, PUT and DELETE. The latent points also hold: get_device turns every OpenSearchException into None, which triggers the new-device overwrite branch, and 'mac in seen_macs' on a list-valued mac raises TypeError, which is not caught.
  • Tracked: new
  • Issue: DeviceRegistry is built in server.py:1077 and only read by /api/devices/registry. grep finds no caller of enrich_from_dhcp/arp/mdns/ssdp, enrich_with_oui/ja3 or register_device outside the tests. No periodic task fills the index. The web PATCH /api/devices/registry/{mac} (acknowledgeDevice) has no daemon route, and the catch-all proxy exports no PATCH either. A second, latent defect: register_device does a read-modify-write, and get_device turns every OpenSearchException (timeouts included) into None. Once enrichment is wired up, a transient error makes an existing device look new and overwrites its first_seen, hostnames, enrichment and user friendly_name. The enrich_ loops also use mac in seen_macs on Arkime's array-valued source.mac, which raises TypeError (unhashable list) and is not caught by except OpenSearchException.
  • Failure scenario: Mirror mode: the home page (+page.svelte:127-133, 551) renders DeviceGrid and NewDeviceBanner from getRegistryDevices(), which is always []. The device grid stays permanently empty, and /devices/mac/[mac] always returns 404.
  • Fix: Add a periodic enrichment task in main.py, run in an executor: DHCP, ARP and mDNS over the last interval, then OUI. Make get_device re-raise anything that is not NotFoundError. Flatten list-valued source.mac. Add the PATCH route, or drop acknowledgeDevice. (effort M)

docs.title: CR-015 (HIGH) — Routing rules never fire: process_event has no caller
docs.text:
• Where: daemon/services/notification_hub.py:473
  • Verdict: CONFIRMED. grep finds no production caller of process_event. The hub is only reached through api/notifications_hub.py for CRUD and test, which is app['notification_hub']. No alert, device, storage or SMART path dispatches events to it. The web-side web/src/lib/server/notifications.ts is a separate env-configured dispatcher and does not use hub rules. The settings page still shows 'Routing rule created.'
  • Tracked: new
  • Issue: Nothing in production calls NotificationHub.process_event. The only callers are in tests/test_notification_hub.py. The settings/notifications page lets users create rules such as 'alert -> Discord, min severity high' and shows 'Routing rule created.', but no alert, new-device, storage or SMART path ever sends an event to the hub.
  • Failure scenario: A user sets up a Discord channel, clicks Test (that works), and adds a rule 'alert, min critical'. A critical Suricata alert fires and no notification is ever sent. The delivery log shows only the test message.
  • Fix: Call hub.process_event from the event sources (the alert poller or a smart-alert cycle, new-device detection, the storage and SMART warning paths in main.py). Until that is wired, hide or mark the rules UI as not active. (effort M)

docs.title: CR-016 (HIGH) — Beaconing detection checks only 300 pairs and can exceed max_buckets, then silently returns no beacons
docs.text:
• Where: daemon/services/threat_detection.py:143
  • Verdict: CONFIRMED. detect_beaconing uses a composite with size 300 over (src, dst, port), never paginates, and puts a 10s date_histogram under each bucket. Exceptions are caught and it returns []. /api/threats/* defaults to a 24h window. In bridge mode every outbound flow has the router's WAN IP as source, so only the 300 lexically-lowest (dst, port) pairs are ever checked. The max_buckets overflow is likely on 24h or 7d windows (sub-buckets count toward search.max_buckets), but whether it trips depends on traffic. The truncation alone is certain.
  • Tracked: new
  • Issue: detect_beaconing uses a composite over (src, dst, port) with size 300 and no after_key pagination, so only the first 300 triples in lexical order are checked. Each bucket also carries a 10s fixed_interval date_histogram. Over a 24h or 7d window that can return tens of thousands of sub-buckets, which goes past OpenSearch search.max_buckets (65535). The exception is caught, logged, and returned as [].
  • Failure scenario: A 24h /threats report on a home network: any pair that talks every few seconds (DNS, NTP, telemetry) gives about 8,640 10s buckets on its own, and 300 pairs push the total past 65,535. The query throws too_many_buckets_exception and the page shows 'no beaconing detected'. When the query does succeed, a host whose triples sort after the first 300 is never checked, so its C2 beacon is missed.
  • Fix: Paginate the composite (or prefilter candidate pairs with a terms agg on doc_count >= BEACONING_MIN_CONNECTIONS). Fetch timestamps per candidate pair in a second query, or use a coarser interval scaled to the range. Return an error to the UI instead of [] when the query fails. (effort M)

docs.title: CR-017 (HIGH) — Generated ISM policies never manage a real index, so age-based retention never runs
docs.text:
• Where: daemon/storage/ilm_generator.py:109
  • Verdict: CONFIRMED. The ism_template patterns are zeek-, suricata-, arkime-* and pcap-* (ilm_generator.py:109/181/230; the static ilm-policy.json is the same). Logstash is configured with MALCOLM_NETWORK_INDEX_PATTERN arkime_sessions3-* and OTHER malcolm_beats_* (docker-compose.yml:233-236), and neither matches. No code calls _plugins/_ism/add or sets rollover_alias (grep finds nothing), and every policy starts with a rollover action, which needs a rollover alias on non-data-stream indices. Age-based deletion therefore never runs.
  • Tracked: new
  • Issue: The ism_template patterns are zeek-, suricata-, arkime-* and pcap-. Malcolm, as configured in compose (MALCOLM_NETWORK_INDEX_PATTERN arkime_sessions3-, OTHER malcolm_beats_), writes all Zeek and Suricata data to arkime_sessions3-YYMMDD and host data to malcolm_beats_YYMMDD. None of these match: arkime- needs a dash, but the real name uses an underscore. ism_template also attaches only to indices created after the policy exists, and nothing calls _plugins/_ism/add for existing indices. Every policy also starts with a rollover action. Daily-named indices have no plugins.index_state_management.rollover_alias, so on any index that did match (for example zeek-recovered-* from reindex_from_logs) the rollover fails, the managed index ends up failed after 3 retries, and the delete transition never runs. The static config/opensearch/ilm-policy.json has the same problem.
  • Failure scenario: A user sets hot=7 days in Settings, and the UI reports ILM 'synced'. After 60 days every arkime_sessions3 index is still there, because nothing deletes by age. Data is only ever removed by the 80% and 90% disk-pressure paths, so the retention settings shown in the UI have no effect.
  • Fix: Target arkime_sessions3-* (and malcolm_beats_*) with a policy that has no rollover action: a single state that moves to delete at min_index_age. Attach it to existing indices with POST _plugins/_ism/add/. Because Malcolm puts Zeek and Suricata in the same daily index, either apply one network retention setting, or document that warm/cold cannot be split by index. (effort M)

docs.title: CR-018 (HIGH) — Writing the capture stop flag at 95% has no effect
docs.text:
• Where: daemon/storage/manager.py:109
  • Verdict: CONFIRMED. capture_stop_flag is always the default /tmp/nettap-stop-capture, because neither the retention_config parsers nor main.py override it. /tmp is a private tmpfs in the daemon container (compose tmpfs: /tmp:size=50M). A repo-wide grep finds no reader of that path outside manager.py, and no container mounts it. The 95% 'stop capture' step is a no-op. Combined with the PCAP cleanup that never runs, nothing stops the disk filling.
  • Tracked: new
  • Issue: _set_capture_stop_flag() writes /tmp/nettap-stop-capture. /tmp is the daemon container's private tmpfs (compose tmpfs: /tmp:size=50M), and no other code or container reads that path (a grep finds it only in manager.py). The 'stop capture at critical_threshold' step in emergency_cascade and run_cycle therefore does nothing, and is_capture_stopped() and the resume logic only track the daemon's own flag file.
  • Failure scenario: The disk reaches 95%. The log says 'CAPTURE STOPPED: Wrote stop flag', but pcap-capture, arkime-live, zeek-live and suricata-live keep writing until the filesystem is full and OpenSearch and Redis fail.
  • Fix: Stop capture for real. The daemon already has docker.sock and _docker_cmd in capture_control: run docker stop on nettap-pcap-capture (and arkime-live) at critical, and docker start when usage drops below resume_threshold. Persist that state so a daemon restart does not lose it. (effort S)

docs.title: CR-019 (HIGH) — Filebeat mounts the Zeek and Suricata log volumes read-only, so their logs are never pruned
docs.text:
• Where: docker/docker-compose.yml:290
  • Verdict: PLAUSIBLE. self-verified by gap agent (no separate verifier)
  • Tracked: new
  • Issue: In Malcolm, only filebeat's cron job (clean-processed-folder.py, run every minute) deletes rotated Zeek archives under /zeek/live/logs and Suricata eve files under /suricata. NetTap mounts both volumes :ro (lines 290 and 293). Three things then stop the cleanup: - For Suricata, eve files older than LOG_CLEANUP_MINUTES=360 are eligible, but os.remove fails with EROFS. silent_remove() swallows the error and the script still logs 'Removed old file'. - For Zeek archives (.log.gz), ZIP_CLEANUP_MINUTES defaults to 0 in the 26.02.0 filebeat image and NetTap does not set it, so the archives are never even considered. - Malcolm's zeekdeploy.sh sets zeekctl LogExpireInterval=0, so Zeek never expires them either. Suricata live output rotates hourly to eve-%Y%m%d_%H%M%S.json and is uncompressed. Neither container's own cron deletes anything; Suricata's cron only updates rules. The daemon does not mount these volumes.
  • Malcolm pass adds: In Malcolm, Filebeat owns log cleanup. Zeek's LogExpireInterval=0 (zeekdeploy.sh), and Filebeat's cron clean-processed-folder.py removes old /zeek/live/logs archives (gated by ZIP_CLEANUP_MINUTES) and old /suricata eve files (LOG_CLEANUP_MINUTES). NetTap mounts zeek-live-logs:/zeek/live:ro and suricata-live-logs:/suricata:ro, so silent_remove() swallows EROFS. NetTap also never sets ZIP_CLEANUP_MINUTES (the image default is 0; upstream uses 720), so rotated Zeek archives are skipped even before deletion is attempted.
  • Failure scenario: On a normal home network, hourly eve JSON files (flow, dns, tls, http, alert) and gzipped Zeek archives pile up in Docker volumes on the root NVMe, at hundreds of MB to more than 1 GB per day, forever. The daemon sees disk use climb but cannot reclaim these files. At 80% and then 90% it deletes OpenSearch indices instead, destroying indexed history. In the end the disk fills, OpenSearch writes fail (the disk watermarks are disabled), and ingestion stops. The filebeat logs claim the files were removed, which hides the problem.
  • Fix: 1. Remove :ro from the zeek-live-logs and suricata-live-logs mounts on filebeat. 2. Set ZIP_CLEANUP_MINUTES (for example "120") next to LOG_CLEANUP_MINUTES so rotated Zeek .gz archives get pruned too. 3. Add a check, for example the daemon reporting these volumes' size, so the problem cannot come back silently. (effort S)

docs.title: CR-020 (HIGH) — Two full-PCAP writers fill the disk; Arkime keeps it at 85-90% and the daemon's 'stop capture' flag is never read
docs.text:
• Where: docker/docker-compose.yml:509
  • Verdict: PLAUSIBLE. self-verified by gap agent (no separate verifier)
  • Tracked: Partially: PR #144 follow-up 'PCAP cleanup path' (the daemon cannot delete PCAP…
  • Issue: arkime-live writes full PCAP of all traffic on PCAP_IFACE to pcap-data/arkime-live. It runs with ARKIME_LIVE_CAPTURE=true and pcapWriteMethod=simple, and live_capture.sh runs capture with -o pcapDir=/data/pcap/arkime-live. At the same time, pcap-capture's netsniff-ng (PCAP_ENABLE_NETSNIFF=true) writes a second full copy to the same volume. CLAUDE.md specifies PCAP as alert-triggered only. The Arkime viewer's expireCheckDevice deletes Arkime's own files only when free space drops below freeSpaceG. ARKIME_FREESPACEG is unset, so it defaults to 10%. That holds the filesystem at about 85% used (ext4 with 5% reserved blocks) or about 90%, which sits on the daemon's thresholds: 80% tiered prune, 90% emergency, 95% critical. At 95%, StorageManager._set_capture_stop_flag() writes /tmp/nettap-stop-capture. That path is inside the daemon's own private tmpfs, and nothing reads it (grep finds no consumer), so capture never stops.
  • Failure scenario: 1. Within days at typical home traffic, Arkime PCAP fills the disk to its 10%-free floor. The daemon is then permanently at 80% or above and runs a tiered prune every 5 minutes. 2. netsniff-ng files are never deleted (the tracked PCAP cleanup path), so Arkime keeps deleting its own PCAP to make room until it has none left. 3. Disk use then crosses 90% and prune_emergency() deletes every OpenSearch index, including today's. 4. At 95% the daemon logs 'CAPTURE STOPPED', but Zeek, Suricata, Arkime and netsniff keep writing until the disk is 100% full and the stack stops ingesting. The two writers also double NVMe write load, against the SSD-endurance design goal.
  • Fix: 1. Keep one PCAP writer. Either drop netsniff, or turn off Arkime PCAP writing and keep its SPI. 2. Set ARKIME_FREESPACEG high enough to leave headroom below the daemon's thresholds, for example 25%. 3. Make the critical-disk path actually stop capture, for example by having the daemon stop the capture containers through the docker socket, instead of writing a flag file nobody reads. (effort M)

docs.title: CR-021 (HIGH) — Arkime viewer runs on host port 8005, and its admin S2S token can be forged with the public fallback secret
docs.text:
• Where: docker/docker-compose.yml:513
  • Verdict: PLAUSIBLE. self-verified by gap agent (no separate verifier)
  • Tracked: new
  • Issue: arkime-live uses host networking and Malcolm's viewer config sets viewHost=0.0.0.0 and viewPort=8005. In live mode, Malcolm's docker_entrypoint.sh (lines 187-196) comments out userNameHeader and userAuthIps, so Arkime 5.8.3 falls back to authMode=digest. viewer/config.js also starts Auth with s2s:true, and serverSecret falls back to passwordSecret (common/auth.js lines 135-141). initarkime.sh:79 creates the user 'admin' with the superAdmin role. Its digest password is random (--webauthonly), but the s2s strategy accepts any x-arkime-auth token that is encrypted and HMAC-signed with sha256(passwordSecret), is less than 2 minutes old and names a matching path. The compose file falls back to the public value 'NetTap_Arkime_Secret' whenever docker/.env has no ARKIME_SECRET. malcolm-config.sh:316-319 skips all .env generation when docker/.env already exists, so any .env that was created earlier never gets ARKIME_SECRET. NetTap's own code never uses the viewer, and no default install path firewalls port 8005 (see the install.sh finding).
  • Failure scenario: 1. An operator creates docker/.env with PCAP_IFACE=eth2, as the compose header tells them to. Another way in: scripts/remote/deploy-phase4-full.sh runs on a fresh clone and does echo MGMT_IP=... >> docker/.env. 2. The operator runs install.sh. malcolm-config.sh logs 'Docker .env already exists, skipping generation'. 3. arkime-live starts with passwordSecret=NetTap_Arkime_Secret. 4. Any host on the management LAN builds x-arkime-auth: <iv>.<AES-256-CBC({date:now,user:'admin',path:'/api/sessions/pcap/...'})>.<HMAC> with key sha256('NetTap_Arkime_Secret') and sends it to https://:8005. 5. The viewer accepts it as superAdmin 'admin'. The attacker can search every session and download full-content PCAP of all traffic behind the bridge: other household devices, plaintext HTTP/DNS, credentials. They can also manage Arkime users and inject sessions or PCAP through /api/sessions/receive. With a random secret the viewer is still an unneeded admin service open to the LAN. DHCP caution: if a new mode sets ARKIME_LIVE_CAPTURE=false (netsniff plus offline Arkime), Malcolm keeps userNameHeader=x-forwarded-user with userAuthIps=::,0.0.0.0/0. Then a plain X-Forwarded-User: admin header gets full access with no secret at all.
  • Fix: 1. Make the secret mandatory: ARKIME_PASSWORD_SECRET: "${ARKIME_SECRET:?ARKIME_SECRET must be set}". 2. Change generate_compose_env so it adds each missing key (ARKIME_SECRET, REDIS_PASSWORD, PUID/PGID, heap sizes) to an existing docker/.env, instead of skipping the whole file. 3. Stop exposing the viewer: bind it to 127.0.0.1, for example by having the entrypoint sed viewHost in config.orig.ini, or drop port 8005 on non-loopback interfaces. Keep the viewer process running, because it is what expires Arkime PCAP. 4. Never run Arkime with ARKIME_LIVE_CAPTURE=false without also removing userNameHeader and userAuthIps. (effort M)

docs.title: CR-022 (HIGH) — Grafana is reachable without NetTap login, with anonymous viewer and default admin password 'nettap'
docs.text:
• Where: docker/docker-compose.yml:824
  • Verdict: CONFIRMED. GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_PASSWORD=${GRAFANA_ADMIN_PASSWORD:-nettap} is set, along with GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_ENABLED=true with the Viewer role. malcolm-config.sh generate_env writes docker/.env without GRAFANA_ADMIN_PASSWORD, and no other script or env file supplies it to compose. generate-secrets.sh writes only to /opt/nettap/.env. nginx /grafana/ has no auth_request.
  • Tracked: new
  • Issue: GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_PASSWORD falls back to 'nettap'. malcolm-config.sh writes docker/.env (the file compose reads) without GRAFANA_ADMIN_PASSWORD. generate-secrets.sh writes it to /opt/nettap/.env, which nothing reads. GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_ENABLED=true with the Viewer role. nginx exposes /grafana/ with no auth_request.
  • Malcolm pass adds: GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_PASSWORD falls back to nettap. malcolm-config.sh never writes GRAFANA_ADMIN_PASSWORD into docker/.env. scripts/generate-secrets.sh does generate one, but writes it to /opt/nettap/.env, which compose never reads (the repo is ~/NetTap and compose uses docker/.env), and install.sh doesn't call it. Grafana is proxied at https:///grafana/ with anonymous Viewer enabled.
  • Failure scenario: Any LAN host browses to https://nettap.local/grafana/ and views dashboards anonymously, or logs in as admin/nettap. As admin it can create data sources pointing at any container on the compose network (opensearch, redis, the daemon via host.docker.internal), use Grafana's datasource proxy, and add users, all without a NetTap account.
  • Fix: Generate GRAFANA_ADMIN_PASSWORD in malcolm-config.sh generate_compose_env, remove the ':-nettap' fallback (use ':?' so compose fails if it is unset), set GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_ENABLED=false, and put /grafana/ behind the same auth_request as /dashboards/. (effort S)

docs.title: CR-023 (HIGH) — --dry-run --persist writes the real netplan bridge, NetworkManager and sysctl configs
docs.text:
• Where: scripts/bridge/setup-bridge.sh:403
  • Verdict: CONFIRMED. The --persist block has no dry-run guard. It writes /etc/netplan/10-nettap-bridge.yaml, /etc/sysctl.d/99-nettap-bridge.conf, nettap-bridge.service and the NM unmanaged conf with plain cat >. Only the systemctl calls go through run(). No early exit for dry-run exists before that block. install.sh defaults PERSIST_BRIDGE=true and passes --dry-run through, and its own daemon.json, 99-nettap.conf and nettap.service writes are also unguarded. On the next boot netplan applies the bridge.
  • Tracked: new
  • Issue: The persistence block writes /etc/netplan/10-nettap-bridge.yaml, /etc/sysctl.d/99-nettap-bridge.conf, /etc/systemd/system/nettap-bridge.service and /etc/NetworkManager/conf.d/99-nettap-unmanaged.conf with plain cat >, not through run(). install.sh passes --persist by default along with --dry-run, and also writes nettap.service, daemon.json and 99-nettap.conf unguarded (install.sh lines 230, 270, 377).
  • Failure scenario: An admin previews with sudo scripts/install/install.sh --dry-run (or setup-bridge.sh --wan enp1s0 --lan enp2s0 --persist --dry-run). Nothing is bridged now, but the netplan file and the NM 'unmanaged' config are on disk. At the next reboot, networkd enslaves both NICs into br0 with dhcp4: false and NM leaves them unmanaged. If either NIC is the current uplink (normal before rewiring), the box comes up with no network.
  • Fix: Guard every file write and apt/systemctl side effect with the dry-run check (log the content instead of writing it), the same way run() does for commands. (effort S)

docs.title: CR-024 (HIGH) — (( applied++ )) under set -e kills the installer at the first ISM policy
docs.text:
• Where: scripts/install/deploy-malcolm.sh:601
  • Verdict: CONFIRMED. I reproduced it in a bash 5.1 container: set -euo pipefail; a=0; (( a++ )) inside an if-body exits with rc=1. apply_ilm_policy is called unconditionally from start_services -> deploy_malcolm -> top level, with no \|\| or if wrapper and no ERR trap. install.sh (set -e) calls deploy-malcolm.sh as a plain command in step_malcolm, so install aborts before step_systemd. That fits DEPLOYMENT-ISSUES Fix 3, where nettap.service had to be created by hand.
  • Tracked: new
  • Issue: deploy-malcolm.sh runs with set -euo pipefail. In bash 4.1+, (( applied++ )) with applied=0 evaluates to 0 and returns status 1, which trips errexit. The same happens with (( failed++ )) at lines 622, 625 and 629. apply_ilm_policy is reached from start_services -> deploy_malcolm outside any conditional, so errexit is active.
  • Malcolm pass adds: deploy-malcolm.sh and install.sh both run set -euo pipefail. In apply_ilm_policy, (( applied++ )) (and (( failed++ )) at 625/629) evaluates to 0 the first time, returns status 1, and errexit kills the script. Verified on bash 5.1, the Ubuntu 22.04 version: set -e; a=0; (( a++ )); echo after exits 1. macOS bash 3.2 does not exit, which hides the bug in development. Separately, _wait_for_opensearch_http gives up after 120s and its non-zero return also aborts under set -e, although the healthcheck itself allows 180s.
  • Failure scenario: Default sudo scripts/install/install.sh (immediate bridge): after 'nettap-hot-policy applied successfully' deploy-malcolm.sh exits 1 with no error message. install.sh (set -e) then aborts in step 4, so nettap.service is never written (no boot persistence), mDNS and the verification steps never run, and only one of the three ISM policies is applied. If the first PUT fails, (( failed++ )) exits the same way.
  • Fix: Use applied=$((applied + 1)) / failed=$((failed + 1)), or (( ++applied )), at all four sites. Add a bats/shellcheck-style test that sources the function with stubbed docker. (effort S)

docs.title: CR-025 (HIGH) — nettap.service ExecStop runs 'docker compose down', so every reboot recreates OpenSearch and breaks auth
docs.text:
• Where: scripts/install/install.sh:397
  • Verdict: CONFIRMED. The failure is real, but ExecStop down is not the root cause. Malcolm's opensearch entrypoint runs setup-internal-users.sh on every container start, including a plain restart. That script rebuilds roles_mapping.yml from roles_mapping.yml.orig with envsubst. ROLE_ADMIN is not set in NetTap's compose, so yq deletes every mapping, and setup-post-start.sh then pushes the result with securityadmin.sh. After any reboot malcolm_internal has no role, so container_health.sh (curl --fail https://localhost:9200) gets 403. With ExecStop down the containers are also recreated through compose, so the depends_on chain (daemon needs opensearch healthy, capture services need the daemon healthy) keeps capture from starting. Removing ExecStop alone would not fix the 403. The real fix point is the missing ROLE_ADMIN in the opensearch environment (docker/docker-compose.yml around line 99). DEPLOYMENT-ISSUES Known Risks records this as observed on the device.
  • Tracked: DEPLOYMENT-ISSUES Known Risks: 'OpenSearch security bootstrap not automated on…
  • Issue: The unit runs docker compose down on stop. That runs on every shutdown, reboot and systemctl restart nettap, and it removes every container. On boot up -d creates a fresh nettap-opensearch, whose roles_mapping.yml reverts to empty (Chain 11). container_health.sh then gets 403 and OpenSearch is unhealthy. The daemon depends_on opensearch healthy, and zeek-live, suricata-live, pcap-capture and arkime-live depend_on the daemon being healthy. The device's untracked scripts/remote/nettap.service has the same ExecStop.
  • Failure scenario: Power cycle or sudo reboot -> containers are removed -> the new OpenSearch returns 403 -> compose reports 'dependency failed to start: nettap-opensearch is unhealthy' -> no capture container starts and every page is empty. The inline appliance silently records nothing until someone SSHes in and runs fix-opensearch.sh.
  • Fix: Change ExecStop to docker compose stop (or drop it and rely on restart: unless-stopped) so containers survive reboots. Add an ExecStartPost that runs the security bootstrap idempotently. Make the capture services independent of daemon/OpenSearch health (they only write to local volumes). (effort S)

docs.title: CR-026 (HIGH) — Documented firewall hardening blocks nettap-web from reaching the daemon
docs.text:
• Where: scripts/install/setup-firewall.sh:225
  • Verdict: CONFIRMED. nettap-storage-daemon uses network_mode: host. nettap-web calls DAEMON_URL http://host.docker.internal:8880 (host-gateway, the bridge gateway IP), so that traffic is local and goes through the INPUT chain on br-. setup-firewall.sh runs ufw default deny incoming plus ufw deny in to any port 8880 on all interfaces, which drops it. SECURITY.md:63 and docs/admin-guide/configuration.md:145 tell users to run the script. Published container ports go through DOCKER/FORWARD, not ufw INPUT, so the mgmt-only allow rules for 80/443 have no effect.
  • Tracked: new
  • Issue: nettap-web reaches the host-networked daemon at host.docker.internal:8880, the compose network gateway. That traffic enters the host INPUT chain on the br- interface. setup-firewall.sh sets ufw default deny incoming and ufw deny in to any port 8880 on all interfaces, and only allows ports on MGMT_IFACE. SECURITY.md and docs/admin-guide/configuration.md tell users to run it. UFW also does not filter Docker-published 80/443, so the 'mgmt only' rules for nginx have no effect.
  • Failure scenario: A user follows SECURITY.md and runs sudo scripts/install/setup-firewall.sh --enable. Every daemonFetch from nettap-web times out (SYN dropped by ufw-user-input), so all dashboard pages fail, setup and bridge calls fail, and Go Live breaks. ufw default deny routed would also drop all forwarded traffic in a future routed/DHCP-gateway mode.
  • Fix: Before the deny, allow 8880 from the compose network subnet: ufw allow in on br-+ to any port 8880 proto tcp, or allow from the docker subnet. Drop the blanket 8880 deny for docker interfaces. Document that Docker-published ports bypass UFW (use DOCKER-USER rules instead). Revisit deny routed for gateway mode. (effort S)

docs.title: CR-027 (HIGH) — The System page bypass control reads active but the daemon sends bypass_active, so bypass cannot be turned off there
docs.text:
• Where: web/src/lib/api/bridge.ts:37, web/src/lib/components/BridgeStatus.svelte:124
  • Verdict: CONFIRMED. The daemon's handle_bypass_status returns only {bypass_active}. The proxy passes it through unchanged, and getBypassStatus returns res.json() typed as {active, activated_at}. BridgeStatus.svelte (mounted on /system) decides at line 124 between disableBypass and enableBypass using bypassStatus?.active, and renders the badge and button from it. active is always undefined, so the card always shows Inactive / Enable Bypass and can never call disable.
  • Tracked: new
  • Issue: BypassStatus is {active, activated_at}. The daemon's GET /api/bridge/bypass/status returns only {"bypass_active": bool} (daemon/api/bridge.py:128). BridgeStatus.svelte (on /system) reads bypassStatus?.active for the badge, the warning text, the button label, and to decide between enableBypass and disableBypass (line 124). bridge.test.ts:267 mocks the shape the daemon never sends.
  • Failure scenario: The admin clicks Enable Bypass on /system. The daemon sets bypass and turns promisc off on both NICs. On the next refresh the card still says 'Inactive' with an 'Enable Bypass' button, while the header badge shows health_status 'bypass'. Clicking again calls enable again. Bypass cannot be disabled from /system, so capture stays off until the user finds the Go Live page, which reads health.bypass_active.
  • Fix: In BridgeStatus, derive the state from health.bypass_active (already in /api/bridge/health). Alternatively, have the daemon status endpoint return {active, activated_at}. Then update the test fixture to match. (effort S)

docs.title: CR-028 (HIGH) — Each page load re-sends alert notifications to email and webhook
docs.text:
• Where: web/src/lib/components/NotificationBell.svelte:50, web/src/routes/api/notifications/from-alerts/+server.ts:5
  • Verdict: CONFIRMED. NotificationBell is mounted once in +layout.svelte, and its mount $effect calls GET /api/notifications/from-alerts. That route rebuilds category batches from /api/alerts/smart?limit=50 and calls sendNotification for every batch with maxSev<=2. Nothing deduplicates. sendNotification creates a new id each time, stores it in-app (capped at 200 via unshift), emits it over SSE and sends email and webhook. The default NOTIFY_SEVERITY_THRESHOLD of 3 lets critical and high through. Every full page load or new tab re-sends them.
  • Tracked: new
  • Issue: The bell is mounted in +layout.svelte. Its mount effect calls GET /api/notifications/from-alerts (triggerAlertNotifications, line 42). That route rebuilds category batches from /api/alerts/smart?limit=50 and calls sendNotification() for every critical or high batch, with no dedup and no record of what it already sent. sendNotification gives each one a new id, stores it in-app, pushes it over SSE, and dispatches to email and webhook every time.
  • Failure scenario: One critical 'Malware' category is in the smart alert window, and email and webhook are enabled. The user refreshes the dashboard 10 times, or opens 10 tabs, and receives 10 identical emails and webhook posts. The in-app store gains 10 duplicate unread items. Because it is capped at 200 entries, real notifications get pushed out, and every other open tab gets the duplicates over SSE. It is also a state-changing GET, so any authenticated page load that reaches the URL triggers it.
  • Fix: Remove the client-side trigger. Run the alert-to-notification conversion server-side on a timer (or in the daemon) with dedup: persist the last converted alert timestamp or a hash of (category, window) and skip batches already sent. If a manual trigger has to stay, make it an idempotent POST. (effort M)

docs.title: CR-029 (HIGH) — Alerts page says "No Alerts" when the daemon or OpenSearch fails
docs.text:
• Where: web/src/routes/alerts/+page.svelte:986
  • Verdict: CONFIRMED. getAlerts, getAlertCount, getAlertTimeline, getAlertTopSignatures, getAlertTopIps and getSmartAlertSummary return zeroed objects on !res.ok. getEnhancedCategories and getAlertCategoryDetail catch and return defaults. The daemon returns 502 'OpenSearch query failed' on query errors. fetchAll uses allSettled, so these fake values are all 'fulfilled' and get rendered. The page has no error state, so it falls through to 'No Alerts ... once Suricata is running'. The [category] page shows 'No alerts in X' at line 503 in the same way.
  • Tracked: new
  • Issue: Every alerts client in $api/alerts.ts returns empty data or zeros on a non-2xx response instead of throwing: getAlerts, getAlertCount, getAlertTimeline, getAlertTopSignatures, getAlertTopIps, getSmartAlertSummary, getEnhancedCategories, getAlertCategoryDetail. fetchAll also ignores rejected results. The page cannot tell "no alerts" from "query failed", and shows the empty state "No Alerts. Alerts will appear here once Suricata is running" with all stat cards at 0 and the threat gauge hidden. alerts/[category]/+page.svelte:503 does the same ("No alerts in X"). PR #110 fixed this pattern on other pages, but not on the alerts client.
  • Failure scenario: After a docker compose down/up without the OpenSearch security bootstrap (CLAUDE.md: roles_mapping resets on every recreate), the daemon returns 502 "OpenSearch query failed" for /api/alerts*. The Alerts page shows Total 0 / High 0, no categories, and "No Alerts". A user checking whether they are under attack is told everything is quiet.
  • Fix: Make the alerts clients throw on !res.ok, as PR #110 did for the other clients. In fetchAll and fetchAlerts, set an error state when the table or count calls fail, and show an error banner instead of the empty state. Apply the same change to the category page. (effort M)

docs.title: CR-030 (HIGH) — PCAP downloads through the catch-all proxy are cut off after 10 s in total
docs.text:
• Where: web/src/routes/api/[...path]/+server.ts:35
  • Verdict: CONFIRMED. No web route exists under api/pcap, so /api/pcap/download goes through the catch-all. That calls daemonFetch with the default AbortSignal.timeout(10_000) and streams res.body. Under the fetch spec, aborting after headers errors the readable body, so a stream still running at 10 s is cut. The daemon's handle_pcap_download awaits download_filtered before it returns a FileResponse, and mergecap and tshark each get up to 150 s (pcap_search.py:394,430). An extraction over 10 s therefore returns 502 'Daemon unreachable: ...timeout'. nginx's proxy_read_timeout of 86400 s is not the limit.
  • Tracked: new
  • Issue: proxyToDaemon calls daemonFetch with the default AbortSignal.timeout(10_000) and then streams res.body back. The signal covers the whole fetch, body included, so when it fires undici errors the body stream mid-transfer. /api/pcap/download first runs a filtered extraction across rotated 100 MB files before it sends headers.
  • Failure scenario: A user downloads /api/pcap/download?filter=host 192.168.1.20&from=...&to=... over a 6 h window. If the daemon takes more than 10 s to build the file, the browser gets a 502 'Daemon unreachable: The operation was aborted due to timeout' JSON instead of a pcap. If it starts within 10 s, a slow Wi-Fi client downloading a 100 MB file gets a truncated pcap when the 10 s runs out.
  • Fix: For the octet-stream and pcap paths (or the whole /api/pcap/* prefix), pass a long or no timeout and abort only on request.signal. Keep the 10 s timeout for JSON calls. (effort S)

docs.title: CR-031 (HIGH) — Saving notification settings reports success but discards everything
docs.text:
• Where: web/src/routes/api/notifications/config/+server.ts:43, web/src/routes/settings/+page.svelte:596
  • Verdict: CONFIRMED. POST reads the body into _body, discards it and returns {success:true}. settings/+page.svelte saveNotifications shows 'Notification settings saved successfully.' on res.ok and ignores the server's message. loadConfig reads only env vars (NOTIFY_EMAIL, SMTP_HOST, NOTIFY_WEBHOOK_URL), and neither the nettap-web compose env nor Dockerfile.web sets any of them. The UI therefore claims alerting is configured when it is not.
  • Tracked: new
  • Issue: POST /api/notifications/config reads the body into _body and returns {success:true}. The Settings page (settings/+page.svelte:597) shows 'Notification settings saved successfully.' on res.ok. The config only comes from env vars (NOTIFY_EMAIL, SMTP_HOST, NOTIFY_WEBHOOK_URL), and docker-compose sets none of them for nettap-web.
  • Failure scenario: An admin enters a webhook URL and email, enables email and clicks Save. The page says 'saved successfully'. A reload shows empty fields, and critical alerts never reach the webhook or email. In a security appliance the user believes alerting is on when it is off.
  • Fix: Persist the config (for example a JSON file under /var/lib/nettap-web) and have loadConfig read it, or return 501/400 so the UI cannot show success. (effort M)

docs.title: CR-032 (HIGH) — Security Posture shows grade A / 100% 'excellent' when its data fails to load
docs.text:
• Where: web/src/routes/compliance/+page.svelte:431
  • Verdict: CONFIRMED. All five clients (traffic.ts:334, alerts.ts:189, devices.ts:218, risk.ts:39, investigations.ts:294) return empty defaults on !ok. Every score function returns 100 for empty input, and the catch at line 431 swallows exceptions while the empty initial state stays in place. Either way the page shows a perfect score and the 'excellent' copy.
  • Tracked: new
  • Issue: The page starts with empty data (lines 33-37), and every score function returns 100 for empty input. fetchAll swallows errors ('Graceful degradation — scores will show 100% with empty data'). The clients it calls (getProtocolDistribution, getAlertCount, getDevices, getRiskScores, getInvestigationStats) also return empty defaults on !res.ok instead of throwing. So any daemon failure produces a perfect score.
  • Failure scenario: The daemon is down or OpenSearch is red, so every /api/* call returns 502. The page shows grade A, 100%, 'Excellent security posture. Your network follows best practices across all categories.', 'No alerts detected — your network looks clean' and the recommendation 'Your network security posture looks excellent.'
  • Fix: Have the five clients throw on !res.ok (or check for the default shape). In the catch, set an error state and show 'Could not calculate posture'. Never compute scores from the initial empty state. (effort S)

docs.title: CR-033 (HIGH) — Go Live falls back to eth0/eth1, and the wizard never stores the real NIC names on success
docs.text:
• Where: web/src/routes/go-live/+page.svelte:45
  • Verdict: CONFIRMED. go-live:45-46 falls back to 'eth0'/'eth1'. The wizard writes nettap_wan_iface/lan_iface only when bridgeVerified is true, which happens only on the mock fallback. If the user skipped Verify, Create Bridge sends eth0/eth1. On a host with predictable NIC names that create fails, and the user sees 'HTTP 400', not the daemon's message, because createBridge reads data.error and the daemon's 400 body has no error key. If Verify did run against a working daemon, the bridge already exists, so Go Live jumps to Phase 2 and the wiring guide labels the ports eth0/eth1. The Verification step links to /go-live whatever the capture mode is, and BridgeManager is always registered. The mirror-mode lockout needs eth0/eth1 naming, so that part is narrow, but the core defect holds.
  • Tracked: new
  • Issue: Go Live reads the WAN and LAN names from localStorage and falls back to 'eth0'/'eth1'. The wizard writes nettap_wan_iface/nettap_lan_iface only when bridgeVerified is true (setup/+page.svelte:382), and with a working daemon that never happens (see the verifyBridge finding). It happens only on the mock fallback. A different browser or a private window also loses the names. The wiring guide (lines 298-345) then tells the user to plug the modem into 'eth0', and 'Create Bridge' sends wan=eth0, lan=eth1. The wizard's Verification step links to Go Live in mirror mode as well (setup/+page.svelte:1708). The daemon API always has a BridgeManager (daemon/api/server.py:1024), so Create Bridge works in mirror mode too.
  • Failure scenario: On Ubuntu 22.04 with predictable names (enp1s0/enp2s0), the page tells the user to cable 'eth0' and 'eth1', ports that don't exist. Create Bridge fails with 'Interface eth0 does not exist'. On a host that does use eth0/eth1 (net.ifnames=0, or a VM), a mirror-mode user who follows 'Go Live Setup' bridges their management and capture NICs together and loses access. The netplan files keep it that way after a reboot.
  • Fix: Get the configured WAN/LAN (and mode) from the daemon, for example the saved capture config, instead of localStorage, and never default to eth0/eth1. Hide or disable bridge creation unless the capture mode is bridge, and don't link mirror (or a future DHCP-gateway mode) users to this page. (effort M)

docs.title: CR-034 (HIGH) — Login form action has no rate limit; the only limiter is unused and keyed on nginx's IP
docs.text:
• Where: web/src/routes/login/+page.server.ts:7
  • Verdict: CONFIRMED. The login page form (method=POST, use:enhance) posts to the default action in login/+page.server.ts, which has no throttling. The only limiter is in api/auth/login/+server.ts, and no client code calls that endpoint (grep finds no callers). It keys on event.getClientAddress(). Compose sets PROTOCOL_HEADER and HOST_HEADER but not ADDRESS_HEADER, so the key is the nettap-nginx peer IP. nginx.conf has no limit_req. When the username exists, argon2id runs (memoryCost 65536, timeCost 3). An unknown username returns before any hash runs, which allows a timing check. Both argon2 and getaddrinfo share the libuv pool, so the threadpool-contention DoS is plausible.
  • Tracked: new
  • Issue: The login page posts to this form action, which has no throttling. The 5/min limiter exists only in /api/auth/login, which the UI never calls. It keys on event.getClientAddress(), and ADDRESS_HEADER is not set in compose, so that address is the nettap-nginx container IP and every client shares one bucket. Each attempt with a valid username runs argon2id (64 MiB, t=3) on the 4-thread libuv pool. dns.lookup for daemonFetch's host.docker.internal uses the same pool. Unknown usernames return before any hash runs, which allows a timing-based username check.
  • Failure scenario: A LAN host runs curl -H 'Origin: https://nettap.local' -d username=admin&password=... https://nettap.local/login in a loop with a wordlist. Nothing limits the guesses (about 20-40 per second on an N100). While the flood runs, argon2 jobs fill the threadpool, every daemonFetch DNS lookup queues behind them and the dashboard stalls for real users. Separately, five bad tries on /api/auth/login from anyone lock everyone out of that endpoint.
  • Fix: Move the limiter into $lib/server and call it from both login paths. Key it on the real client by setting ADDRESS_HEADER=x-real-ip (nginx already sends X-Real-IP), add per-username backoff, and run a dummy verify for unknown users. (effort S)

docs.title: CR-035 (HIGH) — Apply Updates shows "Update Complete" after the 10 s proxy timeout while the update is still running
docs.text:
• Where: web/src/routes/system/updates/+page.svelte:282
  • Verdict: CONFIRMED.
